# Unity animation audit

Load for Animator parameters, transitions/interruption, animation events, root motion, or culling.
Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Use `unity:unity-cli` (or the
Editor) to inspect saved controllers/clips and runtime state; this guide adds ownership and
gameplay-correctness checks. Animation cost is owned by
[Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md); this lens covers correctness only.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Parameter contract | Controller parameter names/types from a controller dump or its saved asset; every `Set*`/`Get*` call and cached hash in code | A code-set parameter name or type does not exist in the controller, or code assumes an override controller adds parameters |
| State ownership | Writers per parameter and layer (search the `Set*` calls); reads of Animator state in gameplay rules | Conflicting writers produce wrong state/effects, or Animator-driven gameplay violates a binding domain rule. State queries and intentionally ordered writers alone are valid; architectural separation is otherwise a proposal |
| Transition semantics | Controller dump: Has Exit Time, duration, interruption source for each input-driven transition | The configured exit/interruption/duration behavior breaks an intended action/cancel response. Interpret Fixed Duration in seconds and other durations relative to source-state length/speed; confirm player-visible delay live |
| Pending triggers | Every `SetTrigger` writer against the transitions that consume it, plus cancel/interrupt/disable paths | A trigger has writers but no transition in any layer consumes it, or a canceled/disabled action fires later after re-enable (live run) |
| Event safety | Clip events: function names, receiving components, clip reuse across states | An event names a function absent from every component on the same object, or required cleanup runs only from an event on a clip that can be interrupted or looped |
| Root-motion writer | `applyRootMotion`, any `OnAnimatorMove`, and the physics/controller writers on the same object | Root motion and another writer conflict on the same pose, or a runtime `applyRootMotion` toggle re-initializes the Animator and causes an unintended state change (confirm live). `OnAnimatorMove` takes control of root motion; an ignored `applyRootMotion` flag alone is no finding |
| Controller/override lifetime | Search `runtimeAnimatorController` assignments and `new AnimatorOverrideController` | A shared mutable override leaks actor-specific mappings, or a controller swap loses required state; shared mappings and a swap alone are valid |
| Culling correctness | `cullingMode` per Animator against gameplay that reads its events, root motion, or bone transforms | The configured culling mode suppresses a required event, root-motion result, or bone update and changes gameplay offscreen (confirm the specific behavior live); mode plus dependency alone is a candidate |
| Clock alignment | `updateMode`, scaled/unscaled time, pause policy, physics and root-motion timing | The selected clock freezes required animation or disagrees with intended collider/movement timing (confirm live); choose mode per actor/use case |

## Interpret with care

- ℹ️ Cache frequently used hashes according to project conventions, then verify their controller
  contract. A cached hash does not prevent typos and should not serve as a stable save identifier.
- ℹ️ Exit time and deliberate transition duration can be correct. The `SetTrigger` reference says a
  trigger returns to false automatically, but does not say when or what consumes it, and its example
  calls `ResetTrigger` on the other trigger first. Reset a trigger when the ownership contract requires
  canceling pending work; `ResetTrigger` before every `SetTrigger` is not a universal fix.
- ℹ️ Animation events can time presentation/hit windows, but interruption still needs reliable state
  cleanup. Inspect invulnerability, hitboxes, reservations, and audio/VFX on every exit path.
- ℹ️ Shared override controllers are useful only when their mappings should be shared. An actor-specific
  mutable mapping may require its own instance. The reference documents that swapping an
  `AnimatorOverrideController` based on the same controller does not reset the current state; it does
  not state parameter behavior, so verify that on the installed engine.
- ℹ️ `AnimatorCullingMode` documents `AlwaysAnimate` (animated even offscreen), `CullCompletely`
  (animation disabled when renderers are not visible), and `CullUpdateTransforms` (retarget, IK, and
  transform writes disabled). The page states no default and does not mention root motion, so treat
  culling first as a behavior decision and verify root-motion and event needs live. Measure any cost
  change with [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md) before editing culling.

## Validation

Play the real action, cancel/interrupt it at relevant points, disable/re-enable, switch clip sets,
and move offscreen. Verify exactly-once effects and reliable cleanup. Use the actual collider/mover
for root-motion checks.

Persisted controller/clip edits must use Unity's Editor APIs; see
[Editor tooling](UnityEditorToolingInstructions.md).

Technical references: [Animator.applyRootMotion](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Animator-applyRootMotion.html),
[AnimatorCullingMode](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AnimatorCullingMode.html), and
[Animator.runtimeAnimatorController](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Animator-runtimeAnimatorController.html).

Additional references: [transition duration/interruption](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-Transition.html),
[update clocks](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AnimatorUpdateMode.html). Skinned deformation
and visibility bounds are checked in [Rendering](UnityRenderingInstructions.md).

# Unity assembly and build-boundary audit

Load for compilation boundaries, Editor/player isolation, tests, or package references. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Respect the project's assembly policy,
including an explicit no-asmdef choice. Use `unity:unity-cli` (fallback: the Editor's compile and
build commands) for validation. **Last verified: October 2026.**

This lens owns test inclusion, normal-player isolation, and Editor folders under an asmdef. Stripping
and AOT belong to [Assets and memory](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md); [Testing](UnityTestingInstructions.md)
links here for inclusion.

## Establish effective boundaries

Map each reviewed script to its effective assembly and platform constraints, including parent
asmdefs, asmrefs, predefined assemblies, package assemblies, and precompiled plugins. Read actual
references and defines. Folder names alone do not establish compilation boundaries once asmdefs apply.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Player isolation | `UnityEditor` usings and types, enclosing `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, effective assembly, platform filter | A `using UnityEditor` (or a `UnityEditor` type) sits in an assembly with no Editor-only filter and no `UNITY_EDITOR` guard; confirm with a compile of a normal player target (needs a build) |
| Editor folder under an asmdef | Scripts in an `Editor` folder and their effective assembly | The folder sits under a runtime asmdef with no Editor-only asmdef or asmref, so only the folder name isolates the code |
| Platform filters | `includePlatforms` and `excludePlatforms` in every `.asmdef` | Both arrays hold values (the file-format reference requires `includePlatforms` to be empty when `excludePlatforms` has values), or an assembly meant to be Editor-only lists any platform besides the Editor |
| Reference resolution | `references` in every `.asmdef` and `.asmref`; the `guid:` in each asmdef `.meta` | A `GUID:<hash>` or an assembly name matches no asmdef in the project or its resolved packages, or one `references` list mixes the GUID and name forms (the reference requires one form per list) |
| Reference direction | The reference graph built from `references`, plus actual source dependencies | A cycle exists in the graph, or a binding project dependency rule is violated |
| Test inclusion | Test asmdefs, every non-test asmdef's `references`, the output of a normal player build or its build report | A normal player build or build report contains a test assembly, or a non-test asmdef lists a test asmdef, NUnit, or `UnityEngine.TestRunner` in `references`; the build-side half needs a build |
| Optional packages | `manifest.json` / `packages-lock.json`, asmdef `references`, `versionDefines`, `defineConstraints` | An asmdef references a package assembly that the project treats as optional, with no `versionDefines` plus `defineConstraints` guard, so it cannot compile when the package is absent |
| Granularity | Editor compile log or `unity:unity-cli` compile timing after a one-file edit | A recorded recompile of one assembly follows an edit that none of its dependents use, and the timing is large enough to matter to the project's iteration goal; report the measurement, never a script count (needs a live compile) |

ℹ️ AOT and stripping findings belong to [Assets and memory](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md).

## Interpret with care

- ℹ️ Absence of asmdefs is not itself a correctness defect. Recommend a boundary for a concrete
  dependency or build problem, with migration cost; avoid script-count thresholds.
- ℹ️ `autoReferenced` defaults to true and controls references from predefined assemblies. It does not
  mean every asmdef references the library. Judge the intended visibility rather than requiring one
  global value.
- ℹ️ An empty `rootNamespace` does not make existing namespaces incorrect; verify in the installed
  Editor what the field controls. Naming belongs to [the style guide](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/UnityStyleGuide.md).
- ⚠️ `UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS` appears in Unity's file-format reference only as an example
  `defineConstraints` value; the manual does not describe what it does. Unity's manual says test assemblies
  are not part of the regular build pipeline and ship only for Play Mode tests run in a Player, but verify
  that in the installed Editor. A missing or present constraint alone proves nothing: decide by a player
  build or build report.
- ℹ️ Interfaces can resolve dependency cycles, but moving a type to Core is appropriate only if Core
  owns that contract. Sometimes an artificial boundary should be consolidated.

## Validation

Compile both the Editor and a representative normal player target for affected boundaries. Verify
relevant test discovery with [Testing](UnityTestingInstructions.md); test-player inclusion is a
separate case. Report build-only checks as Not verified if no build was run.

Technical references: [Assembly definitions](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definitions-intro.html),
[file format](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definition-file-format.html), and
[creating assemblies and test assemblies](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assembly-definitions-creating.html).
Use the installed Test Framework version for exact assembly requirements.

# Unity asset and memory audit

Load for asset loading/release, retained memory, import cost, or build content. Addressables rows
apply only when `com.unity.addressables` is installed; bundle and atlas rows apply only when the
project uses Addressables, AssetBundles, or SpriteAtlas. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Import recipes belong to skills such as
`unity:optimize-audio` and `unity:manage-sprite-atlas` when available, or to
[project presets](../Presets/README.md). This lens owns audio import/residency and streaming-readiness findings; `unity:optimize-audio`
owns implementation recipes, [Audio](UnityAudioInstructions.md) owns playback correctness, and
[Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md) owns measured CPU/DSP cost.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish ownership

Map asset acquisition, consumers, retention, and release for each relevant lifetime. Distinguish
managed wrappers from native asset memory, source assets from runtime instances, and intended caches
from leaks. Follow serialized references transitively; a small configuration asset can retain large content.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Load ownership | Handles, multiple loads/acquires, sharing, replacement | A consumer uses an asset after its release call, or the code that must release a handle no longer holds it |
| Failure/cancellation | Completion and cleanup after disable/destroy/request replacement | A failed load leaves its handle unreleased, or a late result is consumed with no owner to release it (async lifetime is checked in [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md)) |
| Instantiation (Addressables only) | Addressables creation path, clones, instance release | An instance is released through a different path than the installed package requires, or a dependency is released while an instance still uses it |
| Runtime resources | Materials, textures, render targets, meshes, SO clones | `Renderer.material`/`MeshRenderer.material`, `new Material`, `new Texture2D`, `new Mesh`, or a `RenderTexture` is created in code with no `Destroy`/`Release` on a matching teardown path (grep, then trace) |
| Shared configuration | Runtime writes and nested referenced assets | Runtime writes leak consumer-specific/session state into shared configuration or saved authoring data; intentionally shared mutable state with an explicit lifetime/reset contract is valid |
| Import residency | Actual platform format, size, Read/Write need, mips, audio role | An importer's platform size, Read/Write, or mip setting exceeds the project's stated budget or its [presets](../Presets/README.md) with no runtime need; with no stated budget, report sizes and record "no budget" |
| Bundle/atlas dependencies | Build layout, duplicate dependencies, content grouping | Build layout and representative load/release cycles show avoidable duplication or churn that violates a budget/content lifetime. Intentional small duplication or independently used bundle members can be a valid coupling tradeoff |
| Shipping content | Build report, Resources, stripping/preservation, platform overrides | The build report lists content with no reference path, or a type used by reflection or serialization is missing from a stripped build (needs a build to confirm) |
| Audio readiness | Load type, preload/background loading, clip load state, target memory/CPU/I/O and first-use latency | Required playback is delayed by unloaded data, or the import strategy breaks a measured target budget; evaluate streaming/decompression by role and platform, with no universal clip-duration cutoff |

## Ownership cases to verify

- ⚠️ Match each acquired Addressables reference to its owning release path, including failed
  operations: Unity's handle documentation says to release the handle even when the operation failed.
  Check instantiation against the installed package's documented instance-release API, and verify in
  that package whether an `Object.Instantiate` clone of a loaded asset affects the source handle.
  Retain dependencies until their users are finished.
- ⚠️ For any load whose caller can be canceled, name who consumes or releases the eventual result.
  Cancellation and request lifetimes belong to [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md).
- ⚠️ Releasing a handle does not guarantee immediate physical unloading: Unity's Addressables memory
  documentation says released assets are not unloaded at once, and a bundle unloads when its
  reference count reaches zero. Inspect remaining owners and bundle grouping before labeling resident
  content a leak.
- ⚠️ A ScriptableObject created/cloned for runtime use can legitimately hold runtime state with an
  explicit reset/disposal contract. Verify that nested referenced assets of a clone are still shared
  rather than copied, and are safe to share.
- ⚠️ `Resources` content ships in builds. Judge its actual size/use and the project's policy. A small
  deliberate use does not by itself justify an Addressables migration.
- ⚠️ CPU-readable copies, mipmaps, audio streaming, compression, and stripping are workload/platform
  choices. Avoid universal percentages, fixed clip-length rules, or blanket UI mipmap bans.

## Validation

Compare memory snapshots across repeated load/use/unload cycles after comparable warmup. Inspect
surviving reference chains and expected cache lifetime; higher residency alone is not proof of a leak.
Read import values back after reimport and verify appearance/playback on the target platform. Read
the build report for shipping-content claims. Mark measurements not performed as Not verified.

General allocation/frame cost belongs in [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md);
GUID/serialized migrations in [Editor tooling](UnityEditorToolingInstructions.md).

Technical reference: [Addressables package documentation](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.addressables@latest),
and its asynchronous operation handles page. Use the project's installed package for exact release
and platform behavior.

Additional references: [audio import tradeoffs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/class-AudioClip.html),
[duplication tradeoffs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assets-avoid-duplication.html), and
[runtime asset management choices](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/assets-managing-introduction.html).

# Unity audio audit

Load for runtime mixer routing, volume settings, pooled/overlapping voices, spatial sound, or
scene persistence. Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard).
`unity:audio-setup-mixers` owns routing setup and `unity:optimize-audio` owns import/DSP tuning recipes;
[Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md) owns audio import, memory, and streaming findings.
Without those skills, use the checks below and the official docs.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Routing contract | `outputAudioMixerGroup` on every AudioSource in saved prefabs/scenes, and in pooled and one-shot setup code | A shipped source has no mixer group in saved data and no runtime assignment on any path that plays it, where the project routes audio through a mixer. Read the pool and one-shot setup code first: a pooled source whose `outputAudioMixerGroup` is assigned in code is routed |
| Volume units | Slider handlers that call `SetFloat`, and the exposed parameter's units | The slider’s units/range do not match the exposed parameter: linear amplitude reaches a dB parameter without conversion, or a logarithmic conversion accepts zero without a guard. An already-dB slider may pass its value directly |
| Parameter control | Exposed names in code against the `.mixer` asset (mixer dump), the `SetFloat` return, the call site | A missing exposed parameter or incorrect timing prevents applying required settings. An ignored `SetFloat` return is a candidate when no other validation protects the contract; call from Start or later under the documented API |
| Voice ownership | The pool's get/reset path and any voice cap | A checkout inherits mutable state from a previous voice, or the intended active-voice limit is enforced only by the pool’s inactive `maxSize`. Pool-wide invariant properties need not be rewritten every checkout |
| Pool return | What triggers return to the pool | Return runs after a fixed wait of the clip length while pitch, pause, time scale, or loop can change. Cancellation and stale checkout: [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Spatial contract | `spatialBlend`, `minDistance`/`maxDistance`, rolloff on world-space sources | Effective rolloff/curve and spatial settings violate the intended positional/range contract or a binding policy (confirm live). Suspicious min/max values alone are candidates; interpret their meaning for the installed rolloff mode |
| Listener/session state | Enabled `AudioListener` components across all loaded scenes; code that sets `AudioListener.pause` or `volume` | The count of enabled listeners across loaded scenes is not 1, or code sets listener pause/volume with no restore path |
| Settings reapply | Saved volume values and the call that applies them after load; music owner creation | Loaded settings never reach their playback owner, or scene entry duplicates persistent music. A surviving mixer/owner need not reapply settings on every scene start when values remain correct |
| Pause/completion identity | `Pause`/`UnPause`, `isPlaying`, listener pause, `ignoreListenerPause`, scheduled/loop playback | A paused voice is returned because `isPlaying` is false, a required resume is lost, or UI/audio violates the agreed pause policy |
| Voice priority | Real/virtual voice limits, priorities, representative overlap on target | Critical cues/dialogue become inaudible under supported concurrency; priority/voice counts alone do not prove failure and priority behavior differs on Web |
| Music clock | DSP scheduling, clip readiness, lead time, pause/resume | A gapless/rhythm requirement fails through measured gaps/drift or late starts; ordinary sound effects need not use DSP scheduling |

## Cases worth explicit inspection

- ⚠️ A common convention maps a 0.0001 to 1 slider to decibels with `20 * Log10(v)`, which gives -80 at
  the floor; Unity's own sample can instead use a dB slider and pass it straight through. This is a
  convention, not an engine rule. Label the slider contract and handle silence and range explicitly.
- ⚠️ `AudioMixer.SetFloat` returns false if the exposed parameter is not found or snapshots are being
  edited, and the reference says to call it from `Start` or later, not `Awake` or `OnEnable`. After a
  scripted `SetFloat`, snapshots no longer control that parameter until `ClearFloat`. A snapshot
  transition does not simply override every scripted setting.
- ⚠️ The `AudioListener` reference states you can only have one listener in a Scene. With additive
  scenes, count enabled listeners across the whole loaded world.
- ⚠️ A fixed wait of clip length assumes pitch, pause, time scale, loops, and playback ownership stay
  compatible. Match completion/cleanup to actual playback.
- ℹ️ Reverb placement, pitch randomization, stereo/mono, and rolloff shape are design/platform choices
  rather than automatic defects.

## Validation

Exercise mute/volume extremes, restart and scene changes, overlapping sounds, pause/resume, changed
pitch, loops, and cancellation during playback as applicable. Listen on the target setup; inspect
voice/checkout counts after repeated cycles. Verify saved mixer/source wiring and re-read settings.

Technical references: [AudioMixer.SetFloat](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Audio.AudioMixer.SetFloat.html)
and [AudioListener](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioListener.html).

Additional references: [paused isPlaying](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource-isPlaying.html),
[listener/DSP pause](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioListener-pause.html),
[priority](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource-priority.html), and
[scheduled playback](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource.PlayScheduled.html).

Spatial reference: [rolloff-dependent maxDistance](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource-maxDistance.html).

# Unity cameras and cinematics audit

Load for owned camera-follow logic, Cinemachine, Timeline/PlayableDirector or cinematic handoffs.
Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish camera/output
owners, target movement clocks, package versions and supported scene entry paths. A plain camera
alone is a weak signal. Render-pass/stack correctness belongs in [Rendering](UnityRenderingInstructions.md).
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Target sampling | Target movement/interpolation, camera/brain update mode and actual frame order | Camera samples the wrong pose and creates visible jitter/latency that violates the intended behavior; no single update mode fits every mover |
| Manual update | Manual brain/update caller relative to target movement | Missing or duplicate update produces an incorrect pose; a documented custom player loop is valid |
| Camera selection | Brain channel masks, priority/activation and split-screen ownership | The wrong camera/player controls an output; highest priority alone does not bypass channel filtering |
| Cinematic wiring | Saved track/scene bindings, supported entry scene and runtime replacements | Required track/target bindings fail in actual playback; preview success alone does not prove player wiring |
| Handoff lifetime | Camera/input authority on completion, skip, interrupt, failure and scene exit | Cinematic exit strands input/camera ownership or restores a stale prior owner; general lifetime rules stay in [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Clock/lens continuity | Pause/time scale, damping, blending, projection, cuts and teleports | A supported transition violates the intended camera/comfort contract or retains stale smoothing; damping values are design choices |

## Interpret with care

Cinemachine recommendations depend on the target's movement and package version. Multiple brains
can be intentional. A camera cut may require different continuity behavior from a smooth follow;
require the project's desired result rather than a universal damping reset. Timeline rows are
behavior/ownership checks, not claims about a particular binding API. Accessibility motion settings
are reviewed in [Localization/accessibility](UnityLocalizationAccessibilityInstructions.md).

## Validation

Use actual gameplay playback: slow/fast render and physics rates, pause, cuts/teleports, cinematic
completion, skip/interrupt and scene unload. Include two outputs where supported. Reopen saved
bindings and run the agreed player path; unavailable live/player checks are Not verified.

Technical references: [Cinemachine Brain](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.cinemachine@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/CinemachineBrain.html)
and [Rigidbody interpolation](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody-interpolation.html).
Research inspected Cinemachine 3.1.7; Cinemachine 2 and other systems need their own installed contracts.

# Unity defect diagnosis

Load when the user reports a symptom: a Unity runtime/Editor discrepancy, a lifecycle failure, or a
build-only defect. This is a diagnosis mode, not an audit lens: it starts from a reported failure
rather than a review scope, and has no `Finding when` checks of its own. It routes the symptom to the
lens that owns the evidence, then closes with a probe and a regression test. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard) to the final report. Use the available
Editor/IDE tools rather than assuming the agent cannot inspect a debugger.

If a bug-diagnosis skill is available, follow its loop. Otherwise use this one: **reproduce** the
failure, **hypothesise** one cause at a time, **probe** to separate the suspected cause from an
alternative, **fix** the cause, then add a **regression test** that failed before the fix.

## Capture the failing context

Record expected versus actual behavior, exact trigger, first relevant error/stack, engine/package
version, platform/backend, scene/prefab, and recent changes. Distinguish saved authoring state from
live runtime state and the component, scene, action, or request identity involved. Confirm logs
belong to this reproduction rather than a previous compilation/Play session. Record Play state,
compilation/reload state, activity (gameplay, recompilation, preview, or test fixture), log cursor or
timestamp range, and source revision plus relevant dirty-file state per collection. Reuse shared
context and record differences per finding. Retain supplied or measured context as known; mark only
unavailable fields Not verified.

Before implementation, state the observed failure, cause assessment (established, suspected, or
unknown), intended outcome, and checkable acceptance condition. Separate containment from recovery:
a guard preventing invalid callbacks does not establish that gameplay recovers after recompilation.
A probe must distinguish the proposed cause from alternatives; observing an exception alone cannot.

## Route the symptom

| Symptom | Evidence that distinguishes causes | Owning guide |
|---|---|---|
| Null/missing Unity reference | SerializedProperty, required/optional contract, prefab overrides, runtime assignments, destroyed-object check | [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) (destroyed objects), [Editor tooling](UnityEditorToolingInstructions.md) (saved references) |
| Second Play/re-enable breaks | Reload settings, mutable statics, subscriptions, registries, pending requests | [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Input/UI misfires | Actual action instance/phases, update mode, live tree, focus/picking, propagation, domain entry point | [Input](UnityInputSystemInstructions.md), [UI Toolkit](UnityUIToolkitInstructions.md) |
| Contact/query wrong | Actual collider/body pair, layers, query count/capacity, physics synchronization | [3D Physics](UnityPhysicsInstructions.md) or [Physics2D](UnityPhysics2DInstructions.md) |
| Action/effect late or doubled | Animator state/parameters, interruption, event receiver, gameplay effect owner | [Animation](UnityAnimationInstructions.md) |
| Silent/misrouted audio | Source/listener state, group/parameter identity, playback/voice owner | [Audio](UnityAudioInstructions.md) |
| Missing/wrong rendering effect | Effective renderer, camera/pass order, graph resources, shader output | [Rendering](UnityRenderingInstructions.md) |
| Cost or memory grows | Comparable player captures, allocation stacks, retained references, repeated-cycle baseline | [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md), [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md) |
| Editor works; build fails | Platform defines, stripping/AOT, included content, effective assembly, initialization path | [Assemblies](UnityAssemblyDefinitionsInstructions.md) |
| Save/load diverges | Schema/version, real capture/load path, prior fixtures, reconstructed identity | [Persistence](UnityPersistenceInstructions.md) |
| Route/arrival wrong | Pending/partial/invalid path, loaded data, destination floor, actor movement authority | [Navigation](UnityNavigationInstructions.md) |
| Locale or access barrier | Actual supported language/input, fallback, glyph/layout, essential cue and option behavior | [Localization/accessibility](UnityLocalizationAccessibilityInstructions.md) |
| Remote state diverges | Topology, sender authority, durable state, spawn and delivery order | [Networking](UnityNetworkingInstructions.md) |
| ECS state races or disappears | World/group ordering, job dependency, ECB scope/playback and baked content | [Entities](UnityEntitiesInstructions.md) |
| Terrain seam/contact differs | Tile neighbors, authored edges, collider data and height synchronization | [Terrain](UnityTerrainInstructions.md) |
| Camera/cinematic control sticks | Target clock, selected output, saved bindings and interrupted ownership handoff | [Cameras/cinematics](UnityCamerasCinematicsInstructions.md) |

## Traps to keep in view

- ⚠️ The destroyed-object trap (`UnityEngine.Object` wrapping a destroyed native object, and why `?.`
  and `??` miss it) is owned by [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md). A caught exception or
  blanket null guard can hide missing required wiring rather than explain it.
- ⚠️ A prefab's source reference can differ from the scene instance. Inspect the instance that fails
  (see [Editor tooling](UnityEditorToolingInstructions.md) for saved-reference checks).
- ⚠️ An Editor-only repair, static cache, or already-loaded asset can hide a build/startup defect.
  Reproduce from a clean entry path (see [Assemblies](UnityAssemblyDefinitionsInstructions.md)).
- ⚠️ Fixing a visible symptom is not proof of cause. Use a probe that distinguishes the suspected
  owner/order/state from an alternative; record what evidence rules the alternative out.

Re-run the original trigger and verify the exact symptom. Remove temporary probes and restore changed
diagnostic settings. Take result freshness and coverage standards from
[Testing](UnityTestingInstructions.md).

# Unity design audit

Load for responsibility, dependency, state-machine, or command-boundary review. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Use `unity-project-review` for general
pitfall review when it is available; this guide stands alone and adds questions about actual ownership.

⚠️ Design findings are **proposals**, not defects, unless a rejected or repeated operation produces
wrong state. Report those two kinds separately: a confirmed defect carries an inspected invalid-state path or reproduced wrong state;
a proposal carries the countable trigger below plus its tradeoff.

## Establish the design

Read relevant domain documentation and recorded decisions. Map the command entry point, the owner
of its rules/state, composition, collaborators, and consumers. Trace representative success,
rejection, cancellation, and teardown paths. Judge complexity at the caller's interface, including
required setup and ordering, rather than by file size or interface count.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| One policy owner | The same rule in UI, simulation, preview, and save/load | Two implementations of the rule return different results for the same input, or one fix must be repeated in 2+ callers |
| Complete command | Validation, mutation, resource charging, registration, and events | A rejected operation leaves partial state, charges twice, or publishes success before commit |
| Valid state | Collection exposure and every mutation entry point | External mutation bypasses an invariant, or required setter ordering permits invalid observable state; public mutability alone is a proposal under the project policy |
| State transitions | Allowed transitions, entry/exit effects, pending work | Re-entry, repeated requests, or interruption produces stale effects or an impossible state |
| Explicit dependencies | Constructors, serialized wiring, bootstrap, discovery calls | A hidden dependency or required initialization order causes an inspected failure, violates a binding dependency policy, or makes a scoped test require unrelated global setup; discovery/static access alone is a design candidate |
| Dependency direction | `.asmdef` reference lists, `using` directives, and serialized asset references of reusable (Core) code | A reusable assembly or namespace references game-specific content or presentation (count the references; each one is a candidate) |
| Useful abstractions | Callers and actual implementations | A forwarding abstraction adds demonstrated caller/setup or maintenance cost without hiding a volatile boundary; one implementation alone is not evidence that an interface is unnecessary |
| Observable contracts | Return results, units, valid inputs, failure meanings | An operation returns `void` or a bare `bool` and N call sites read a field, catch an exception, or re-query state to learn whether it succeeded |

For a command that spends a resource and changes world state, trace the real entry point: a rejected
request must leave the resource, world state, and success events unchanged; a success must apply the
agreed effects exactly once. Adapt that check to the project's actual rules rather than introducing
a generic transaction framework.

## Interpret with care

- ℹ️ Composition-time injection can use concrete collaborators. Introduce an interface when it hides
  a volatile boundary or solves a demonstrated substitution/testing need.
- ℹ️ Direct calls suit owned collaborators; events suit observers. Audit event ownership and lifetime
  with [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md), rather than prescribing a global event bus.
- ℹ️ An enum/switch can be the clearest state machine. Recommend classes only when they reduce
  transition or per-state complexity. A singleton's risk is hidden scope/lifetime, not its name.
- ℹ️ ScriptableObject configuration and runtime state need explicit ownership; see
  [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md). Shared event-channel assets need a session reset contract.
- ℹ️ Consolidation and deletion may improve a design more than splitting another manager. Preserve
  existing behavior and serialized identity when changing ownership.

## Recommendation

For each proposal, name the current owner, intended owner, smallest interface, concrete benefit, and
migration cost. State that crossing a save boundary belongs to
[Persistence](UnityPersistenceInstructions.md). A proposal is complete as an audit result when its
evidence and tradeoff are clear; implementation belongs to the selected follow-up work.

# Unity Editor tooling and asset-integrity audit

Load for custom tools, serialized changes, migrations, or asset-integrity review. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). `unity:unity-cli` owns safe Editor
execution (fallback: the Editor's own menus and batch mode); `unity:ui-uitk` / `unity:ui-imgui` own UI
implementation. Project asset-editing guardrails remain in `AGENTS.md`. **Last verified: October 2026.**

This lens has two parts. Run the [Integrity pass](#integrity-pass) for every whole-project audit and every
metadata-touching change. Load [Tool authoring](#tool-authoring) only when the project owns Editor tooling.

## Integrity pass

Always on for a whole-project audit and for any change that touches `.meta` files, serialized assets, or
renamed fields. Skip it for a change that touches none of those. It is read-only, combining static metadata checks with Editor-assisted reference/type checks.
Read metadata and serialized references as evidence, never hand-edit them. Account for ignored paths, packages,
deliberate optional references, and import state before calling something broken. List every affected
asset pair for a duplicate GUID, including vendor metadata when it participates in the same database.

Move-time GUID checks belong to [ReviewFolders](../FolderStructure/ReviewFolders.md). The settings that keep
`.meta` files visible and tracked belong to [ProjectSettings](../ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.md) and
[SetupVersionControl](../VersionControl/SetupVersionControl.md); this pass checks metadata content.

| Check | How to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate GUIDs | `grep -rh "^guid:" --include='*.meta' Assets Packages \| sort \| uniq -d`, then grep each duplicate to list every `.meta` that holds it | Any `guid:` value appears in more than one `.meta` |
| Missing or orphan metadata | For each path under `Assets` and embedded `Packages` (scan only `Assets` and embedded `Packages`; skip folders ending in `~`, hidden folders whose name starts with `.`, and copies such as agent worktrees, `Library`, or build output), check `<path>.meta` exists; for each `.meta`, check its asset exists | An asset has no `.meta` after the Editor has imported the project, or a `.meta` has no asset; files added while the Editor was closed are not findings until it opens |
| Null or unresolved scripts | Grep saved scenes, prefabs, and assets for `m_Script: {fileID: 0}`; read one saved MonoBehaviour for the exact reference form, then resolve each script GUID against the project's `.meta` files | `m_Script` is `fileID: 0`, or a script GUID resolves to no `.meta` and no deliberate optional-package guard. Unity's built-in resource references (all-zero-prefix GUIDs such as `0000000000000000e000000000000000` and `0000000000000000f000000000000000`, used by built-in shaders, fonts, and materials) are expected and not findings; no official list of them was found, so confirm what a reference points to in the installed Editor before excusing it |
| Missing references | A `unity:unity-cli` Editor query for missing scripts and missing object references over scenes and prefabs (discover the installed command first) | A count above zero for any asset; each is a finding unless documented as optional. Needs a live Editor: record Not verified otherwise. Static fallback: every `guid:` referenced by first-party scenes, prefabs, and assets resolves to a `.meta` in scope (built-in references excepted); an unresolved GUID is a candidate missing reference |
| Managed-reference types | Hosts using `[SerializeReference]`; `SerializationUtility.HasManagedReferencesWithMissingTypes` in an Editor query | Required data has an unresolved managed type after namespace/class/assembly changes; preserve recoverable serialized data and diagnose the missing type before proposing a migration |
| Tracked generated content | `git ls-files Library Temp obj Logs UserSettings` | Any generated folder has tracked files |

## Tool authoring

Load only when the project owns Editor tooling: custom EditorWindows, Inspectors, or drawers, menu or batch
migrations, `OnValidate` or `InitializeOnLoad` code, or scripts that use Undo. Otherwise record Not applicable.
With many tools, sample by risk (tools that act on open scenes or prefab instances, or that write many assets) and state the sample instead of inspecting every file.

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Serialized identity | Diff of renamed or moved serialized fields, `FormerlySerializedAs` use, enum member lists, saved assets | A renamed field has no migration attribute or script while saved assets still hold the old name (grep the old name in `.asset`, `.prefab`, `.unity`), or an enum member's number changed and a saved asset reads back as a different member |
| Inspector edits | `SerializedObject` / `SerializedProperty`, `Update`, `ApplyModifiedProperties`, or binding | An Inspector writes `target` fields directly without those calls or without Undo, bypassing multi-object editing, prefab overrides, or Undo |
| Tool edits | `Undo.*` calls before each change, `SetDirty`, prefab-instance modification recording | A tool that acts on open scenes or prefab instances mutates an object with no `Undo.*` call before the change, or an Undo/Redo run leaves the change in place, or a prefab-instance edit is not recorded. A missing `Undo.` call is only a candidate elsewhere: batch tools that load, change, and save assets do not need it |
| Asset operations | `System.IO` and `AssetDatabase` calls on `Assets/` paths | A tool moves, copies, or deletes files under `Assets/` with `System.IO` instead of `AssetDatabase`, or a `.meta` pair is broken after it ran |
| Batch safety | `StartAssetEditing` / `StopAssetEditing` or `AssetDatabase.AssetEditingScope` | A `StartAssetEditing` has no matching `StopAssetEditing` in a guaranteed `finally`, or an `AssetEditingScope` is created outside a `using` statement without a guaranteed `Dispose` |
| Migration scope | Target filter, preview or dry-run mode, a second run on a throwaway copy, result log | The filter reaches unselected package or vendor content, there is no preview, a second run changes assets again (diff it), or completion is reported with no per-asset failure list |
| Editor callbacks | `OnValidate`, `InitializeOnLoad`, `InitializeOnLoadMethod`, reload hooks | `OnValidate` reaches a non-thread-safe operation, or initialization uses imported assets before they are available. File I/O/scans in `InitializeOnLoad` are cost/reload-safety candidates, not automatic defects |
| Serialization callbacks | `ISerializationCallbackReceiver` implementations and their helper calls | A callback reaches main-thread-only Unity APIs or depends on an undocumented ordering between managed-reference siblings; keep conversion local to owned fields |
| Saved result | `SetDirty`, `SaveAssets`, read-back after reload, git diff on a throwaway copy | A tool that must ship its change never calls `SetDirty`/`SaveAssets`, or the git diff is empty after the tool ran, or a reopened scene or prefab lacks the change |

## Cases worth explicit inspection

- ⚠️ `SerializedProperty` editing through ApplyModifiedProperties/binding already manages normal Undo
  and dirtying. Direct non-inspector edits need the appropriate Undo API before mutation, plus
  prefab-instance recording and scene/asset persistence appropriate to the object.
- ⚠️ Creation, component addition, hierarchy changes, and destruction may need specialized Undo APIs;
  `Undo.RecordObject` alone is not a complete transaction for every tool action.
- ⚠️ `FormerlySerializedAs` lets a renamed field keep its saved value
  ([reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Serialization.FormerlySerializedAsAttribute.html)).
  Unity's docs reviewed here do not describe enum numbering or when the attribute is safe to remove, so treat
  existing enum numbers as part of the saved format and prove changes with a read-back of saved assets.
  Removing migration support needs evidence that all supported content has migrated, not a time limit.
- ⚠️ `OnValidate` can run when scripts load or values change, including on threads other than the main
  thread. Keep it to validating the data that changed; schedule scene and asset operations through a safe
  Editor path.
- ⚠️ A migration should identify intended targets, record failures, avoid overwriting unsaved work,
  and distinguish already-correct content. Pause imports with `AssetDatabase.AssetEditingScope` in a `using`
  statement, or `StartAssetEditing` / `StopAssetEditing` inside `try`/`finally`; unbalanced calls leave
  imports paused ([reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AssetDatabase.AssetEditingScope.html)).
- ⚠️ When a result must be committed, inspect saved asset references and the diff. Reopen representative
  scenes/prefabs, including variants/overrides. A screenshot or runtime hierarchy proves only that state.

## Validation

For tools, exercise Undo/Redo, multi-selection if supported, prefab instances/variants, cancel/failure,
and rerun where applicable. Re-read saved output and verify GUID/reference identity after reload.
Do not save an unrelated dirty scene to make a tool check pass. Keep live-only or unopened assets
Not verified. Editor/player compilation boundaries belong in
[Assemblies](UnityAssemblyDefinitionsInstructions.md).

Technical reference: [OnValidate](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnValidate.html).

Serialization references: [missing managed types](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/SerializationUtility.HasManagedReferencesWithMissingTypes.html)
and [callback threading/order](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/ISerializationCallbackReceiver.html).

Initialization reference: [InitializeOnLoad asset availability](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/InitializeOnLoadAttribute.html).

# Unity Entities correctness audit

Load for owned Entities systems/jobs, bakers, EntityCommandBuffers or SubScenes. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish package version, worlds,
system groups, player/baking paths and resource owners. Installed Entities alone is weak evidence.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| World/order | Effective world/group, creation versus update order, producer/consumer dependencies | A required producer is absent or runs too late; relative update attributes are assumed to constrain systems outside their supported same-group scope |
| Job dependencies | Scheduled handles, reads/writes, state dependency propagation and completion | Data is consumed/disposed while a job still uses it, or a required dependency is lost; Complete alone is not a defect |
| Deferred entity scope | ECB temporary entities and their consumers | A temporary entity is used with EntityManager or another ECB before valid playback remapping |
| Playback visibility | Producer completion, ECB playback/disposal and downstream consumers | Playback races a producer or a consumer expects structural changes before they become visible |
| Resource/world lifetime | Native containers, world/system creation and teardown, repeated Play | Owned resources survive beyond their intended world/session, are disposed twice, or remain in use at disposal |
| Baked/shipped state | Required components/references in authored SubScenes versus clean player load | Live baking masks missing runtime components/content or a player consumes invalid entity references |

## Interpret with care

Creation order and update order are different contracts. Inspect the actual world and group tree;
attributes alone are not proof. ECBs defer structural changes and have their own entity scope and
playback lifetime. Framework-managed cleanup can satisfy ownership; do not demand a second disposal
path. General native-container cost belongs in [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md).
DOTS Physics contacts/step ordering and Netcode for Entities prediction/ghost baking exceed this
lens; record those specialist checks Outside coverage unless separately reviewed.

## Validation

Inspect the actual Systems window/order, use available safety/race checks, and exercise spawn/despawn,
world disposal/recreation and SubScene unload/reload. Validate required baked content in a normal
player. Static scheduling inspection does not prove race freedom; absent live/build checks are Not verified.

Technical references: [system groups/order](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.entities@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/systems-update-order.html),
[ECB scope and safety](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.entities@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/systems-entity-command-buffers.html), and
[job scheduling](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.entities@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/systems-scheduling-jobs.html).
Research inspected Entities 1.3.15; newer package behavior must be matched to installed source.

# Unity Input System audit

Load for action/map ownership, UI/gameplay arbitration, one-shot input, device changes, or rebinding.
Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Inspect existing action assets
through `unity-cli` (the `unity:unity-cli` skill, when available) as needed; retain the project's
chosen integration style. This lens owns UI/world arbitration; the UI lenses link here.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish effective input

Read Active Input Handling, installed package version, update mode, actions/interactions/processors,
PlayerInput/device pairing, and UI input integration. Identify whether an action instance is owned,
shared through an asset/reference, or copied per player. One input asset or one enabled map is not a
universal requirement; the key is intentional ownership and consumption.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Enable ownership | Enable/disable paths and every shared consumer | A required map is disabled, or one consumer disables another's input |
| Callback ownership | Delegate identity, phases, cleanup, registration paths | A `performed +=`/`canceled +=` registration has no matching removal with the same delegate, or a disabled/destroyed consumer still reacts after re-enable (delegate-lifetime rules: [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md)) |
| Interaction semantics | Action type (Button/Value/PassThrough) against its binding interactions and processors | An interaction is configured on an action whose type the installed package does not apply it to (list each action type against its interactions in the asset, then confirm in the package manual), or cached input is read without handling the canceled/neutral phase |
| Timing | Configured update mode (Dynamic, Fixed, Manual) and where each action is read | The installed package reports an unsupported direct action read for the configured update mode, or the capture/latch/consume path loses or repeats a one-shot (live run: frames with zero and multiple fixed steps). Capturing in Update and consuming a latched value in FixedUpdate is valid when each input is consumed exactly once |
| UI/world arbitration | Action maps/modes, focus, UI input integration, input consumers | A menu, text field, or modal interaction also triggers a gameplay action (live run), or UI integration deviates from the checks below. Element-side picking/focus: [UI Toolkit](UnityUIToolkitInstructions.md) or [uGUI](UnityUGUIInstructions.md) |
| Device scope | PlayerInput copies, control scheme, InputUser pairing | A global device read serves the wrong player/device or violates the documented pairing contract; an intentional global shortcut or diagnostic read is valid |
| Rebinding | Completion/cancel/error, enable-state restoration, persistence | A `RebindingOperation` is not disposed on every exit, gameplay actions fire during rebinding, or the action's pre-rebind enable state is not restored |
| Generated code | Source asset/generation settings and owned wrapper disposal | The generated wrapper differs from the action asset, or an owned wrapper instance has no `Dispose` at its owner's end |

## UI integration checks

These come from Unity's [Input System UI support](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/UISupport.html)
manual (checked against package version 1.14); confirm against the installed package's manual.

- ⚠️ From Unity 2023.2 UI Toolkit does not need the UI Input Module component. If a module is present,
  its settings take priority over the UI settings in the project-wide actions, so a stale module can
  silently override them.
- ⚠️ To stay compatible with UI Toolkit, keep the UI action map's name, its action names, and its
  action types unchanged. Pointer and tracked-device actions are PassThrough; Submit and Cancel must be
  Button.
- ⚠️ Calling `EventSystem.IsPointerOverGameObject` from an action callback such as `performed`
  produces a warning because UI state reflects the previous frame; poll it in `Update` instead.
- ⚠️ Do not feed one gamepad to both the Virtual Mouse and the UI module's navigation actions: the UI
  receives the input on two channels and triggers twice.
- ⚠️ Nothing automatically stops gameplay from also receiving input the UI consumed. Check for an
  explicit mechanism: split controls, or a mode switch that disables gameplay actions while UI is active.

## Cases worth explicit inspection

- ⚠️ For cached values, handle neutral/canceled state appropriate to the action type, including mode
  changes and device disconnect. A pass-through action's phase behavior differs from a value action.
- ℹ️ Unity's update-mode setting offers Process Events In Dynamic Update, In Fixed Update, or Manually;
  the manual does not say how to read or latch one-shot input between them. Latching a one-shot from
  `Update` for use in `FixedUpdate` is a common project convention, not a documented rule: verify it
  in the installed version and do not flag all `ReadValue` in `FixedUpdate` as a bug.
- ⚠️ A stored callback can be detached using the same delegate. Re-creating a lambda in cleanup is not
  the same subscription; follow [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) for lifetime ownership.
- ⚠️ Dispose owned generated action instances and rebinding operations (Unity's manual says to dispose
  each `RebindingOperation` so it does not leak unmanaged memory). Shared assets need a shared owner's
  policy; a consumer should not blindly dispose or disable them.
- ⚠️ Restore the pre-rebind mode/enable state on all exits rather than always enabling the action.
  Persistence of overrides and settings belongs in [Persistence](UnityPersistenceInstructions.md).
- ⚠️ Do not infer duplicate events merely from two subscribers or PlayerInput plus custom code; verify
  action-instance identity and whether they both execute the same effect.

## Validation

Exercise press/hold/release, disable/re-enable, map changes while held, pause/modal/text entry,
disconnect/reconnect, and rebind success/cancel when applicable. For commands applied in the physics
step, follow the timing evidence in [Physics](UnityPhysicsInstructions.md). Verify overrides survive
the supported restart path.

Technical reference: [Input System settings](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/Settings.html).
Use the installed package's settings and behavior when deciding timing findings.

# Unity localization and accessibility audit

Load for supported languages/localization readiness, or player-facing UI, controls and information.
Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish supported locales,
platforms, input methods, font/UI systems, and adopted accessibility requirements. Localization and
accessibility are distinct: one language can still have access barriers, and a package install solves
neither by itself. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Content/fallback | Supported locale tables or custom store, text/images/audio, fallback policy | Supported content exposes keys/blanks/wrong assets or lacks the agreed fallback; a missing cell with a valid regional fallback is not itself a defect |
| Formatting | Sentence templates, arguments, plurals, number/date/currency culture | Supported language/count/value produces wrong meaning or formatting errors; equivalent custom formatting is valid |
| Locale lifetime | Initialization, subscriptions, refresh, pending load and locale replacement | Cold startup assumes unavailable data, old results overwrite a newer locale, or visible content fails to refresh; Web startup must not rely on synchronous Localization initialization |
| Script/layout coverage | Glyph fallback, shaping/direction, text expansion, rendered controls | A supported script is missing/incorrect, essential text clips, or text growth makes controls unusable at supported sizes |
| Perceptible information | Essential audio/color cues, subtitles, captions and source/speaker identity | A supported task requires information unavailable through the player's supported settings/input; document the concrete barrier and equivalent cue |
| Operable interaction | Focus/navigation, remapping, hold/mash/drag demands, supported devices | A required task cannot be completed using a supported control path or adopted access option; broader options remain proposals with their audience/tradeoff |
| Readability/comfort | Actual text/backgrounds, scaling, motion/shake/bob and cinematic settings | A demonstrated barrier or adopted requirement fails; numeric contrast/size targets follow the adopted standard and element category |
| Settings ownership | Accessibility/locale values, runtime application, restart and view recreation | An offered setting is inaccessible, lost, or does not change the intended behavior; storage checks belong to [Persistence](UnityPersistenceInstructions.md) |

## Interpret with care

Pseudo-localization screens expansion, untranslated content and formatting issues; it does not prove
real translation, shaping or right-to-left correctness. Test actual supported scripts. Subtitles cover
dialogue; captions can also convey essential non-speech sounds. Assess real gameplay backgrounds,
controls and information rather than the existence of a checkbox. Use platform-owner accessibility
guidelines as a review source; this lens is not legal or platform certification. Classify unadopted
improvements as proposals and state who benefits. UI wiring and input arbitration stay in their lenses.

## Validation

Cold-start, switch locale rapidly, reopen views, remove a translation, and test fallback in a player.
Exercise representative plurals, largest supported text and real supported languages at target sizes.
Complete representative tasks muted, without color differentiation, and through supported alternate
controls. Verify focus restoration and settings after restart. Record absent device/user testing Not verified.

Technical references: [pseudo-localization](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/Pseudo-Localization.html),
[locale refresh](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/Scripting.html),
[formatting](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/Smart/SmartStrings.html),
[initialization/platform limits](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.localization@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/UnityEngine.Localization.Settings.LocalizationSettings.html), and
[Xbox Accessibility Guidelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/accessibility/xbox-accessibility-guidelines/).
Match the installed implementation; research inspected Localization 1.5.13. Platform guidelines are
recommendations unless the project has adopted them as requirements.

# Unity navigation audit

Load for owned NavMesh agents, surfaces, obstacles, links, or path requests. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish engine/navigation package,
agent types, area filters, loaded data, and movement authority. Custom pathfinders need their own
source-matched contracts; package presence alone does not establish NavMesh usage.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Surface/data contract | Saved bake inputs, geometry/layer filters, agent type, loaded surface data | An intended route is absent or unsuitable for the actor in the shipped scene; no universal bake preset is required |
| Request/result contract | `SetDestination`, pending/complete/partial/invalid states, arrival and replacement logic | A submitted request or partial/invalid path is treated as successful arrival; pending or infinite distance is consumed as a completed result |
| Reachability | `SamplePosition` callers, destination constraints and actual path | A nearby point on another floor/disconnected island is accepted where a reachable target is required; sampling proximity alone does not prove reachability |
| Movement authority | Agent pose updates, physics, root motion, `nextPosition` and update flags | Active writers fight, or agent and actor diverge; deliberate one-direction animation/physics integration is valid |
| Obstacle handoff | Agent/Obstacle activation, carving, death/immobilization and pooling | Simultaneously active behavior causes self avoidance/carving or breaks the intended route |
| Route lifetime | Link endpoints, direction, agent type/area, custom traversal, surface unload/rebuild | A supported traversal cannot complete or cancel, or required navigation data disappears while users still depend on it |

## Interpret with care

NavMesh arrival is a gameplay contract, not a universal `remainingDistance` comparison. Check failed,
pending, partial, replaced, and zero-length paths separately. Avoidance does not establish route
reachability. Runtime rebuild and carving frequency are cost proposals under
[Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md). A component combination alone is a candidate.

## Validation

Traverse intended narrow passages, slopes, multilevel/disconnected destinations, both supported link
directions, stop/resume and teleports. Interrupt a request/traversal, unload/reload surfaces, and
reuse pooled actors. Reopen saved bake/link configuration. Missing live route checks are Not verified.
General cancellation/resource ownership remains in [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md)
and [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md).

Technical references: [surface contracts](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.navigation@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/NavMeshSurface.html),
[mixing movement components](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ai.navigation@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/MixingComponents.html),
