# Unity networking and multiplayer audit

Load for owned replication, RPCs, network/session objects or multiplayer lifecycle. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish topology, trusted authority,
package/transport versions, session ownership, targets, and authoritative game rules first. NGO examples
are conditional; third-party stacks and distributed authority need their own installed contracts.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Authority/request validation | Receive-side sender identity, object permission, ranges, rule validation, repeated requests | An untrusted peer can mutate another owner's state or authorize impossible effects; a client-supplied identity alone is not proof of authority |
| Durable state | Spawn/late-join initialization, current replicated state versus transient events | A late/reconnected player misses required persistent state because it existed only in past RPCs; a transient effect need not be replayed |
| Network lifetime | Spawn/despawn, subscription ownership, pool reuse, transfer/disconnect/shutdown | A stale owner/callback acts after despawn, a pool checkout inherits a prior network identity, or shutdown/restart leaves session state behind |
| Delivery/order | Reliability, ordering scope, local/remote execution, tick/time units, prediction if used | Required behavior depends on delivery/order not guaranteed by the installed transport/package, or host and remote paths apply effects differently |
| Connection trust | Authentication versus approval, payload, actual transport protection, credential/log lifetime | Untrusted approval data authorizes a session, or sensitive payload is exposed by the actual protection/logging path; approval alone is not authentication |
| Failure/recovery | Timeout, disconnect, failed join, overlapping session requests, reconnection policy | Failure strands loading/input/session ownership or reconnect duplicates committed state; general async ownership stays in [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |

## Interpret with care

Authority is a topology choice, not a universal server-only prescription. NGO NetworkVariables sync
current state to late joiners; RPCs are transient. Permissions, receive metadata, local RPC timing and
ordering vary by package/version. Treat payloads as untrusted at the authority boundary, even when a
caller-side UI validates them. Retry/deduplication policies should match command semantics rather than
adding a generic distributed transaction framework. Bandwidth/tick changes need measured workloads.

## Validation

Use real remote clients as well as host mode: join in progress, reconnect, transfer/disconnect owners,
despawn/reuse, shutdown/restart, invalid and repeated requests. Add representative latency, jitter and
loss with supported network simulation. Verify authority and exactly-once outcomes, not only smooth
local presentation. Keep missing multi-process/device/backend checks Not verified. This lens is not a
penetration test; backend infrastructure, service authorization and Netcode for Entities prediction
need separately scoped specialist review.

Technical references: [NGO state and late joining](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/basics/networkvariable.html),
[RPC identity/timing](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/advanced-topics/message-system/rpc.html), and
[approval protection limits](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.netcode.gameobjects@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/basics/connection-approval.html).
Research inspected NGO 3.1.0; verify the project's actual package/topology before applying API claims.

# Unity performance audit

Load for frame cost, allocations, pooling, rendering, or jobs. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Use `unity-project-review` for general
pitfall scanning and, when available, an optimization skill such as `unity:optimize-web` for
implementation/tool workflows; without one, use project tooling and official docs.
This lens owns frame cost, including rendering, animation, UI, and audio cost; resource residency
belongs to Assets. [Rendering](UnityRenderingInstructions.md) owns rendering correctness.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish the workload

Identify the target platform, representative scene/action, scale, frame/memory budget, and available
captures. Trace hot paths transitively: frame/physics/render callbacks, per-frame async/coroutine
loops, UI refreshes, and their helpers. A method name or API occurrence alone does not establish cost.
Separate a project rule violation from a measured bottleneck and from an unmeasured risk.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Avoidable hot work | Call frequency, object count, searches, queries, repeated calculations | Measured repeated work breaks the workload budget, or a binding hot-path rule is violated. Search/GetComponent frequency alone identifies a candidate; include scale and caching invalidation cost |
| Managed allocation | GC.Alloc stacks, strings, boxing, closures, LINQ, collection growth | A profiler GC.Alloc sample, or a reached `new` of a reference type/closure/LINQ call, sits on a frequent path and breaks the stated budget or project rule |
| Cache validity | Invalidation and replacement paths | A dirty flag, cached camera/component, or derived value is read after the state it derives from changed without the cache being invalidated (trace each write to the cached source) |
| Query cost | Query volume, masks, ranges, hit needs | Measured unnecessary query scope/result collection breaks a budget or project rule; all-layer masks and collecting multiple hits can be intentional even when one result is ultimately chosen |
| Collection use | Capacity, clearing, iteration, ordering assumptions | Lookup/growth/recreation cost is material at the measured scale or violates a binding rule; a linear scan over a small collection is not automatically an optimization finding |
| Pool cost | Creation bursts, retained objects, reset and active counts | Reuse fails (a new instance per `Get`), retained inactive count grows past `maxSize` expectations, or required concurrency exceeds an explicit cap |
| Rendering | Captures, batching/instancing, overdraw, camera/pass count | A Profiler or Frame Debugger capture (live run required) shows a draw/submission/fill cost with a verified cause |
| Jobs/native containers | Dependencies, completion, allocator lifetime, disposal | A `Complete()` call stalls the main thread longer than the work it offloads (capture), or a container is disposed while a scheduled job still uses it |
| Frame pacing | Platform's vSync/frame-cap behavior and frame-time distribution | A device capture shows frame time above the target (1000 / target fps ms) in the representative scene, or `Application.targetFrameRate` and `QualitySettings.vSyncCount` are set so the cap cannot reach the target |
| Bottleneck attribution | CPU active versus waiting time, render thread, GPU timing, loading and frame caps | A performance conclusion attributes a wait/present marker to CPU overload without establishing the limiting work, or measured active work exceeds the target budget |

## High-value interpretation checks

- ⚠️ `new` on a value type is not automatically a managed allocation. Stored delegates and reused
  collections differ from fresh closures and expanding buffers. Confirm type and call context.
- ⚠️ A reused `StringBuilder` can grow; `ToString()` still allocates. Changing displayed values only
  when needed can be sufficient without complicated zero-allocation formatting.
- ⚠️ Prefer a single-hit query when the caller needs one hit, and use collection overloads only when the
  result contract needs them; check completeness in [Physics](UnityPhysicsInstructions.md). Confirm
  allocation behavior with a capture rather than the overload name, and note that moving a query to
  `FixedUpdate` does not automatically make it cheaper.
- ⚠️ `ObjectPool<T>.defaultCapacity` sets the pool's initial capacity and `maxSize` its retained
  limit; neither is a concurrent-borrower cap. Verify whether instances are prewarmed in the installed
  version: prewarming needs multiple simultaneous checkouts, and a repeated Get/Release loop can keep
  returning the same object. Pool reset and stale async results are checked in
  [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md).
- ⚠️ `MaterialPropertyBlock` and per-renderer material changes have batching tradeoffs. Recommend from
  the actual pipeline and capture, not a blanket replacement. Material instance ownership is checked
  in [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md).
- ⚠️ Immutable cached shader/Animator hashes do not need session resets. Check API availability against
  the installed version rather than copying a Unity 6 rename table.
- ⚠️ Jobs/Burst, GPU Resident Drawer (verify support in the installed pipeline and graphics API), GC
  suspension, batching changes, and extra caches are proposals only when the workload supports them.
  Their overhead or correctness costs can outweigh savings.

## Validation

Measure representative development-player captures on the target device where available. Record
warmup, scene/action, scale, build/backend, capture settings, and comparable before/after conditions.
Report frame-time distribution and spikes, allocation rate, and retained memory as relevant. Editor
captures can locate candidates; keep target-device claims Not verified without device evidence.

Use focused markers to confirm a hypothesis. Deep Profile is diagnostic instrumentation, not a
neutral before/after baseline. Re-measure a selected change and verify its behavior; a lower draw
count or zero GC column alone does not establish an overall improvement.

Measure subsystem cost here, then read the subsystem lens for its correctness checks:
[UI Toolkit](UnityUIToolkitInstructions.md), [uGUI](UnityUGUIInstructions.md),
[Animation](UnityAnimationInstructions.md), and [Audio](UnityAudioInstructions.md).

Technical reference: [ObjectPool constructor semantics](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Pool.ObjectPool_1-ctor.html).

Bottleneck reference: [Highlights Profiler](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/ProfilerHighlights.html).

# Unity persistence audit

Load when reviewing saved game state, in-game settings persistence, save migrations, or load
reconstruction. Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Use the
project's existing save format and tooling; this guide checks data safety without prescribing a
persistence framework. "Settings" here means the player's in-game options, not Unity Player Settings
(`ProjectSettings`). **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish the contract

Identify the snapshot owner, storage location, format/schema version, stable content/entity IDs,
and supported prior versions. Trace capture, write, read, validate, migrate, and reconstruction through
the real save/load entry points. Distinguish a disk save from in-memory state and configuration assets.
Detection and sampling count first-party runtime code, not Editor tools.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Complete snapshot | Saved fields versus player-visible authoritative state | Authoritative state required to reconstruct supported behavior is absent, or transient UI/cache state is treated as authoritative; values recomputed correctly on load need not be stored |
| Stable identity | Entity/content references and reconstruction maps | Runtime instance IDs, list positions, names, or cached hashes silently point at different content later |
| Schema evolution | Version dispatch, prior fixtures, unknown/missing fields | Old data is misread, silently overwritten, or accepted with invalid semantics |
| Write failure | Temporary write, replacement strategy, backup and error handling | Partial I/O can destroy the only good save or report success before durable completion |
| Consistent capture | Concurrent mutations and async snapshot/write requests | Live state can mutate after the first `await` of a snapshot, or two overlapping writes can complete in either order and the older one wins |
| Safe reconstruction | Validation, references, registries, dependency order, events | A failed load partly replaces the live session or reconstructed entities register/apply effects twice |
| Missing content | Removed IDs, absent DLC/mods, corrupt/truncated input | Load crashes or silently assigns unrelated defaults without the agreed recovery behavior |
| Platform lifecycle | Pause/focus/quit policy and storage access, for the project's actual targets | On a target that suspends instead of quitting, the only save trigger is graceful quit. Unity documents that `OnApplicationQuit` may not be called on mobile (iOS suspends instead of quitting) and points suspension handling to `OnApplicationPause` and saving to `OnApplicationFocus`; verify other platforms in the installed version. A desktop-only project may rely on quit or explicit-save paths, so record this row Not applicable per target rather than flagging it |
| Settings | The store holding in-game options (settings file, `PlayerPrefs`, or cloud profile), its read path, and each option's runtime owner | After a fresh start an option value is read from its store but never applied to its runtime owner (a mixer parameter, quality level, or binding), or is shown in the UI without being saved |
| `PlayerPrefs` use | `PlayerPrefs.Set*` call sites and the keys they write | Credentials/tokens or other sensitive data are stored unencrypted there, a Web build exceeds its documented 1 MB limit, or the chosen usage violates a demonstrated save/recovery contract. Small non-sensitive progress values alone are a design choice |

Use a platform-supported safe replacement strategy; renaming a temporary file is not a universal
cross-platform guarantee of atomic or durable writes. Retain the prior good save until the agreed
write/recovery contract succeeds. Report I/O failures with a useful outcome rather than swallowing them.

ℹ️ Unity describes `PlayerPrefs` as storage for player preferences between sessions. It is stored
without encryption, Unity says not to use it for sensitive data, and Web builds keep up to 1 MB in the
browser's IndexedDB. The reference states no general size limit for other platforms; this is not a guarantee of unlimited
storage. Judge progress storage by integrity, recovery, and platform requirements rather than a blanket ban.

## Validation

Test round-trip **behavior**, not just equal field values: save, rebuild a fresh session, then exercise
one command that depends on the saved state. Include a supported older fixture, missing/invalid data,
removed content, write failure, repeated loads, and overlapping saves when those cases apply. Use
temporary storage; verify a failed write leaves recoverable data and a failed load leaves the agreed
session state.

Read [Testing](UnityTestingInstructions.md) for fixture/result standards and
[Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) for async and platform lifetime. Serialization field
renames and enum migrations in Unity assets belong in [Editor tooling](UnityEditorToolingInstructions.md).

Technical references: [`PlayerPrefs`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/PlayerPrefs.html),
[`MonoBehaviour.OnApplicationQuit`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnApplicationQuit.html).

# Unity 2D physics audit

Load for owned Rigidbody2D/Collider2D, joints/effectors, Physics2D queries, or 2D callbacks. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish body types, simulated state,
layers/overrides, trigger settings, physics scene, simulation mode, timestep, and actual saved pair.
The [3D Physics lens](UnityPhysicsInstructions.md) has a different contact/query contract; DOTS
Physics is also separate. **Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Contact eligibility | Dynamic/kinematic/static pair, Full Kinematic Contacts, trigger/layers, callback signature | The configured pair cannot produce the required solid contact/callback under the installed 2D matrix; account for trigger exceptions |
| Movement ownership | Transform/velocity/force/MovePosition writers and automatic/manual stepping | Writers overwrite intended motion, or repeated pre-step MovePosition calls lose intended movement. Ordered contributions and teleports can be valid |
| Step ownership | `simulationMode`, Simulate callers, FixedUpdate and time units | Integration steps twice, is skipped, or consumes input on the wrong cadence. Manual Simulate does not invoke FixedUpdate |
| Query contract | Actual overload, ContactFilter2D, layers/depth/triggers, initial overlaps and returned count | Wrong/self/initial-overlap results are consumed, or required hits are omitted without a capacity policy; inspect the actual overload's ordering contract |
| Callback lifetime | Disabled scripts/objects, pooling and interaction identity | A disabled MonoBehaviour still applies forbidden effects through a 2D trigger callback, or compound hits duplicate one intended effect |
| Fast motion | Required speed/geometry/timestep and collision mode | A supported interaction tunnels or a required contact is missed (live); continuous mode has cost and is not a universal setting |
| Authored geometry | Composite/Tilemap generation, joints and effector configuration where used | Saved geometry/constraints or one-way behavior differs from the required interaction after reopening or runtime changes |

## Interpret with care

Full Kinematic Contacts changes solid-contact eligibility; triggers have different rules. A 2D ray
can report a containing collider at fraction zero with an inverse-ray normal; copying the 3D
ray-origin rule would be wrong. MovePosition is consumed on the next simulation update and has motion
limits; choose cadence from the actual simulation owner. Fixed steps improve repeatability without
proving cross-platform determinism. Input capture belongs in [Input](UnityInputSystemInstructions.md).

## Validation

Test intended body pairs, excluded layers, triggers, start-inside/self queries, saturated buffers,
compound interactions, pause, pooling, and zero/multiple steps per rendered frame. Traverse composite
borders and one-way platforms where used; reopen saved assets. Report unperformed live checks Not verified.
Joint tuning beyond these contracts needs installed documentation and representative solver evidence.

Technical references: [kinematic contacts](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/2d-physics/rigidbody/body-types/kinematic/kinematic-body-type-reference.html),
[MovePosition](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody2D.MovePosition.html),
[manual simulation](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D.Simulate.html),
[ray origins](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics2D.Raycast.html), and
[disabled-script trigger delivery](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Collider2D.OnTriggerEnter2D.html).

# Unity 3D physics audit

Load for Rigidbody motion, collider contacts/triggers, tunnelling, or physics-query results. This
is a 3D PhysX lens: use [Physics2D](UnityPhysics2DInstructions.md) for classic 2D; DOTS Physics
needs its installed package documentation and specialist review. Apply [the shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard).
`unity:physics-3d-collision` (when available) owns detailed collision diagnosis and parameter recipes;
without it, use the checks below and the official docs.
**Last verified: October 2026.** Re-read the linked pages against the installed Editor before quoting
a default.

## Establish the simulation

Inspect the saved and live body/collider pair, layer matrix/overrides, trigger flags, movement owner,
physics scene, simulation mode, and timestep. Confirm callback signatures and target versions.
A script alone does not prove what colliders and bodies exist on its runtime object. A saved
scene/prefab dump or `unity:unity-cli` component listing gives the pair; a live run gives the contact.
A project that uses only kinematic bodies and queries (no dynamic Rigidbody contacts) records the
contact- and force-based rows it cannot trigger (Force units, Effect identity, Fast motion, and
Contact eligibility where no callbacks fire) Not applicable per row instead of failing them; a kinematic
body that raises trigger callbacks still needs Contact eligibility.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Movement ownership | Search for writes to `Rigidbody.position`, `linearVelocity`, `AddForce`, `MovePosition`, and `transform.position`/`Translate` on bodies; add network/teleport paths. List every writer per body. Root motion is owned by [Animation](UnityAnimationInstructions.md) | Active writers overwrite or fight the intended pose/velocity, or a transform write bypasses a simulated body’s movement contract; ordered contributions and deliberate teleports can be valid |
| Force units | `AddForce` mode, and any multiplication by `Time.deltaTime`/`Time.fixedDeltaTime`. One-shot input latching is owned by [Input](UnityInputSystemInstructions.md) | A continuous force mode (`Force`, `Acceleration`) is multiplied by a time step again, or `Impulse`/`VelocityChange` is applied every step where the result should scale with time |
| Contact eligibility | Saved or live collider/body types, trigger flags, layer matrix, callback signatures; compare the pair with the collision-action matrix in the installed version's manual | The layer matrix excludes the pair, a callback kind does not match the collider's trigger flag, or a callback signature takes the wrong parameter type |
| Effect identity | Colliders under each body root and the handlers on each | One interaction can reach a handler through more than one collider and no dedupe key exists; confirm by counting invocations for one interaction in a Play run (needs a live run) |
| Query contract | Mask, radius, `queryTriggerInteraction`, result use | Trigger interaction or mask is left at a default the use case contradicts, or code indexes `RaycastAll`/overlap results as if sorted (Unity documents the order as undefined) |
| Query completeness | Buffer length, returned count, overflow handling in every `*NonAlloc` call | Required all-hit, nearest-hit or post-filter semantics can lose relevant results when a finite buffer saturates without a completeness policy, or code consumes stale slots beyond the returned count. An any-hit boolean or explicit acceptable truncation may already satisfy its contract |
| State synchronization | Transform writes in `Update`/`LateUpdate` followed by a query in the same frame; `Physics.SyncTransforms` calls | A required query observes stale geometry after a pose change, or measured redundant synchronization violates a budget. Inspect actual write/query/simulation order and auto-sync mode; callback name alone is insufficient |
| Fast motion | Max speed, `Time.fixedDeltaTime`, thinnest collider extent on each side, `collisionDetectionMode` per body | Supported speed/timestep/geometry produces a missed required collision (confirm live). Speed × step versus thickness screens tunnelling risk; that estimate or discrete mode alone does not prove failure |
| Collider validity | Collider type, convexity, body type, `lossyScale` chain; Editor console or import output | An unsupported shape/body combination is established, or inspected geometry/contact differs from the intended shape. Non-uniform scale alone is a candidate; unavailable shape inspection is Not verified |
| Query origin | Ray origin versus containing colliders and intended initial-overlap behavior | A ray is expected to detect the collider containing its origin, leaving an inspected interaction/obstruction case wrong; 3D raycasts exclude that collider |
| Visual interpolation | Interpolation/extrapolation, camera follow, physics versus rendered pose, teleports | Observed jitter, overshoot, or latency breaks the required visual/aim contract; interpolation adds a physics-step delay and extrapolation can overshoot |

## Interpret with care

- ℹ️ Use forces/velocity for simulated motion and the supported kinematic movement path for driven
  bodies. Deliberate teleports need an explicit pose/velocity/interpolation contract. A transform
  write does not by itself prove velocity was discarded; inspect the actual movement behavior.
- ℹ️ In `FixedUpdate`, `Time.deltaTime` returns the fixed-step interval, so `Time.fixedDeltaTime`
  expresses intent more clearly; the former alone is not a timing bug. `AddForce` applies timestep
  scaling for continuous force modes, but `Impulse` and `VelocityChange` do not depend on step length.
- ℹ️ Continuous collision detection (CCD) is set on the moving body. The `Continuous` mode detects
  static mesh geometry without a Rigidbody, so do not add a Rigidbody to every wall. The reference
  lists support for sphere, capsule, and box colliders on the body, and recommends `ContinuousDynamic`
  for fast bodies and `Continuous` for the bodies they hit. Verify this against the installed version.
- ℹ️ Non-allocating queries trade allocation for finite result capacity. The reference notes that a
  full buffer is not guaranteed to hold the closest hits, so "count == capacity" needs an explicit
  completeness policy when omitted hits affect correctness. A single-hit `Raycast` overload returns one
  `RaycastHit` through `out`, not an array.
- ℹ️ A radius-based overlap has no max-distance argument. Require a meaningful spatial bound, not
  parameters the API cannot accept. Choose Update/fixed/manual timing from the query's purpose.
- ℹ️ The `Physics.SyncTransforms` reference advises against calling it in `FixedUpdate` (transforms
  sync before each step), for synchronizing changed transforms when an immediate query needs them, and against overuse because it is expensive. Manual physics stepping alone does
  not establish cross-platform determinism; verify on the target platforms.
- ℹ️ Rigidbody API renames (`velocity` to `linearVelocity`, `drag` to `linearDamping`) are tracked in
  [UnityTechStack](../../AgentsInstructions/UnityTechStack/UnityTechStack.md); verify them in the target's 3D and 2D APIs.

## Validation

Reproduce the actual pair and effect. Test representative speed/timestep extremes, compound-collider
hits, full query buffers, layer/trigger exclusions, and teleports where applicable. Verify saved
settings survive reopening. Mark unresolved live geometry/contact checks as Not verified.

Technical references: [CCD and collisionDetectionMode](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Rigidbody-collisionDetectionMode.html),
[Time.deltaTime](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Time-deltaTime.html), and
[Physics.SyncTransforms](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.SyncTransforms.html).

Additional references: [ray origin behavior](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.Raycast.html)
and [interpolation tradeoffs](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/rigidbody-interpolation.html).

Finite-buffer reference: [RaycastNonAlloc results and saturation](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.RaycastNonAlloc.html).

# Unity rendering-correctness audit

Load for owned rendered content: features/passes, shaders, cameras, lighting, LOD/occlusion,
skinned meshes, particles, or VFX Graph. Apply only rows relevant to the selected scene/pipeline. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish the installed pipeline and
version first; the Render Graph rows apply only to the active Render Graph path. Compatibility-mode,
Built-in, and HDRP code need their own installed documentation rather than a forced URP migration.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

This lens owns rendering correctness. [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md)
owns measured frame cost; [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md) owns general residency and
shipping content. Use available pipeline-specific review tooling, or inspect installed source and
Unity's Frame Debugger/Render Graph Viewer. Tool availability alone does not prove rendered output.

## Establish the rendered path

Record Graphics and quality-level pipeline assignments, renderer data and camera renderer overrides,
active features, Render Graph versus compatibility mode, target APIs, and relevant shader/material
assets. Trace an affected camera from pass injection through resource production and consumption to
its final output. Inspect saved settings separately from transient runtime state.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Pipeline and feature wiring | Effective pipeline/renderer per quality level and camera; saved feature/material references | A required feature is missing, disabled, or assigned to an unused renderer and the supported scene loses the intended effect; confirm the active path |
| Pass timing and camera scope | Injection event, camera filters, prerequisites, base/overlay/preview cameras | A pass executes before its required input exists, runs on an unintended camera, or applies an effect twice and changes the intended output (capture/live run) |
| Graph resource declarations | Actual texture/buffer reads and writes versus builder declarations, attachments, and access modes | Execution uses a resource absent from the recorded dependency contract or uses an incompatible access mode; confirm against the installed API and graph validation |
| Graph lifetime | Internal handles, imported external resources, frame/camera transitions, owner cleanup | An internal resource handle is reused across graph instances/frames/cameras, or an external resource is released while a pass still uses it; identify the owner and exact lifetime |
| Recording and execution | Pass data, render function, mutable feature/camera state | Deferred execution observes another camera's or a later pass's mutable data instead of the data recorded for this pass, producing wrong output; inspect captured state and test multiple cameras |
| Output dependency | Consumers of each result, graph culling, global-resource declaration | A required result has no declared consumption/side-effect path and its pass is removed, or a consumer reads a resource before its producer (graph inspection plus output check). An intentionally unused pass being culled is correct |
| Target compatibility | Texture descriptors, dimensions, MSAA/depth/format, shader pass and API requirements | The configured target or shader is unsupported by the selected pipeline/API, or resizing/quality switching produces invalid attachments or wrong pixels; use installed support rules and device/build evidence |
| Camera stacking | Saved base/overlay stack, renderer support, ordering, clear/output policy | The intended overlay is absent, clears required content, or composites in the wrong order; confirm supported stacking in this pipeline/version and the resulting image |
| Shader/material compatibility | Actual material/shader assignment, compile log, required variants in a release player | A supported scene renders an error/missing effect due to a pipeline mismatch, compile failure, or missing required variant. Variant/shipping ownership: [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md) |
| Lighting data/probes | Intended realtime/mixed/baked setup, saved lighting data, loaded scene combinations, supported probe system | Missing/stale data or missing intended probe coverage causes wrong supported output on scene/player load; realtime-only lighting and pipeline-specific probe choices are valid |
| LOD/occlusion | Renderer membership, bounds, thresholds, visibility data, actual quality/camera path | Camera movement hides required visible content or selects incorrect/missing geometry; missing LOD or occlusion alone is a measured-cost proposal |
| Deformation bounds | Skinned/procedural poses, runtime clips, actual culling bounds | Valid deformation leaves bounds and disappears; larger bounds/offscreen updates trade visibility correctness against work |
| Effect simulation | Particle/VFX space, clock, bounds/culling, stop/clear, pause/offscreen and pool cycles | Required effects disappear, move in the wrong coordinate frame, retain old particles on reuse, or never complete their owning checkout; inspect VFX dynamic-bounds recomputation in the installed package |
| Effect capacity/completion | Particle limits, bursts, child/sub-emitter completion and stop/reuse paths | Supported required feedback is dropped at capacity, or checkout completion omits live child effects. Decorative saturation and explicit cancellation can be intentional; judge actual outcome |

## Interpret with care

- Internal Render Graph resources are managed by the graph and cannot be carried between frames or
  cameras. Imported resources remain owned externally; their underlying allocation can persist, but
  import it into the graph that uses it. Retention alone is not a leak.
- Record dependencies and pass data during recording; issue rendering commands in the pass's
  execution function. Inspect the installed APIs for global resources and intentional side effects.
- Graph culling, camera filtering, shader keywords, and compatibility mode are legitimate choices.
  Report a broken contract or binding project-rule violation rather than banning a setting.

## Validation

Use the real scene with the feature enabled and disabled, then test applicable resize, quality/API
switching, multiple cameras, and scene reload paths. Inspect the graph/Frame Debugger and output;

# Unity scenes and lifecycle audit

Load for startup, scene flow, enable/disable behavior, asynchronous work, destroyed-object checks, or
repeated Play sessions. Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Use the
project's lifecycle and composition decisions; inspect live state through `unity:unity-cli` (or project
tooling) when needed. This lens owns pool and async staleness and cancellation checks.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish lifetime ownership

Map application-, scene-, enable-, and request-lifetime owners. Find who initializes, registers,
cancels, and releases each one. Inspect the supported entry scenes and Enter Play Mode settings.
A bootstrap scene is one valid choice; it is not mandatory for every game.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Readiness | Bootstrap/composition path, required services, inactive and spawned objects | A consumed value depends on initialization that is not guaranteed to precede the read, leaving an inspected failure path or a reproduced wrong value. Serialized/default state independent of the other object’s callbacks need not have explicit execution ordering |
| Enable lifetime | Publisher/delegate identity and cleanup paths | A subscription made in `OnEnable`/`Start` has no matching unsubscribe in `OnDisable`/`OnDestroy`, or a Play-toggle of `enabled` doubles a callback count (live run) |
| Registration ownership | Registry entries on disable, destroy, scene exit, and replacement | A registry still holds an entry after its owner's disable/destroy (count before and after), or a removal keyed by type/name rather than owner identity can delete a newer owner's entry |
| Session reset | Mutable statics, static events, caches, SO channels, reload settings | A static field, static event, cache, or SO channel holds state that survives into the next Play and no documented reset policy covers it (see the policy below); confirm with a second Play where a counter or subscriber from the first run is still present |
| Persistence scope | Persistent roots and scene reload behavior | Reloading a scene creates a second instance of a service marked persistent (`DontDestroyOnLoad` with no duplicate guard), or a persistent object keeps references to objects of an unloaded scene |
| Scene transitions | Load/activation/unload order, failure and overlapping requests | An overlapping request or unload/activation ordering loses required scene state, deadlocks a queued operation, or leaves loading/input-block flags set. Unloading first to fit a memory budget is valid with a defined recovery path |
| Active scene | Instantiation and lighting expectations after additive loads | Actual object scene ownership or effective lighting differs from the intended additive-scene contract. Inspect supported explicit destination-scene instantiation, parent placement, SetActiveScene and MoveGameObjectToScene paths; absence of one API alone is not a finding |
| Async ownership | Every await and operation start, cancellation and error observation | Pending work can outlive its consumer with an unsafe continuation or unreleased result, or an operation error has no observing owner. Bounded or intentionally application-owned work need not accept a cancellation token merely because it awaits |

## Async cases that basic null checks miss

- ⚠️ `destroyCancellationToken` covers destruction. Enable-lifetime work needs cancellation on disable;
  request-lifetime work also needs replacement/cancel handling. Create and dispose token sources
  according to that ownership.
- ⚠️ After an await, verify that the result still belongs to the current request. A live, enabled object
  can have been returned to a pool and reused. A generation/request ID can distinguish the old work.
  A pooled object's reset must happen before consumers observe activation.
- ⚠️ Cancellation of a wait does not necessarily cancel its underlying scene/asset operation. Establish
  what completes, who releases the result, and who restores transition state on every exit path.
  The release path itself is checked in [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md).
- ⚠️ A Unity `Awaitable` instance is pooled and should be awaited only once: the Awaitable
  documentation says awaiting more than once is never safe and can throw or deadlock. Shared
  completion needs a deliberately reusable representation. Return to the main thread before accessing
  Unity objects.
- ⚠️ Observe errors at the operation's owner, including fire-and-forget entry points. Do not assume an
  un-awaited `Awaitable` surfaces its exception: the Awaitable documentation does not say it does, so
  verify exception behavior in the installed version.

The [continuation manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/async-awaitable-continuations.html)
now describes thread switching as local to the current async method, with caller-thread resumption.
Older Unity manuals describe different Awaitable continuation behavior. Verify the installed engine
and actual continuation path, especially after explicit thread switches or context suppression;
require a main-thread switch where needed rather than after every await. Background work also needs
an application-exit owner when component destruction alone does not end it.

## Destroyed-object checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Destroyed-object null check | Fields typed `UnityEngine.Object` or a subclass (`GameObject`, `Component`, `ScriptableObject`); callbacks after `OnDestroy`; pooled and async results | `?.`, `??`, `??=` or `is null` is applied to such a field and the guarded access can run after the object is destroyed (grep `\?\.`, `\?\?`, `is null`, then read the caller) |

Unity's `Object` reference says `?.` and `??` are not supported with Unity Objects because they cannot
be overridden to treat detached objects as null, and are safe only when the checked object is
guaranteed never to be detached. It also says a detached object compares equal to `null` while
`Object.ReferenceEquals(obj, null)` returns false. C# [constant null patterns](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/operators/patterns)
bypass overloaded equality, so `is null` does not invoke Unity's destroyed-object check.
Use Unity's `== null` or implicit bool check for
objects that can be destroyed. A hit on an object that cannot be destroyed (a plain C# class, an
`Object` held only by its owner for its own lifetime) is not a finding.

Triage by lifetime: a `?.`, `??`, or `is null` site is a candidate only when the referenced object's
lifetime can be shorter than its holder's (a scene object held by a longer-lived owner, a pooled or
spawned object, an object another system destroys). Scene membership alone does not prove equal
lifetime: a component can be destroyed while its holder
survives. For `GetComponent<T>() ?? AddComponent<T>()`, establish the actual returned reference and
failure path; an Editor allocation observation alone does not establish a detached-object bug.

## Interpret with care

Read the real Enter Play Mode setting before judging session reset. Unity's manual states that the
Editor does not perform a domain reload on entering Play mode by default, and the
[project settings guide](../ProjectSettings/ProjectSettings.md#reload-policy) records the new-project
default as Reload Scene only (domain reload off) and owns the policy. With domain reload off, static
state survives between Play sessions, so a mutable static or static event is a finding when its state
can leak into the next Play and no documented reset covers it. Documented resets are
`[AutoStaticsCleanup]`/`[NoAutoStaticsCleanup]` (documented from Unity 6.5) and the
`[OnEnteringPlayMode]`/`[OnExitingPlayMode]` lifecycle attributes that the manual names. A project that
documents `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration)]` resets is
following a valid policy; do not report it as a conflict. The
[`SubsystemRegistration` reference](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/RuntimeInitializeLoadType.SubsystemRegistration.html)
names `OnCodeInitializing` as the option for new code (better resource pre-allocation timing) and does
not say it resets statics, so verify in the installed version before adopting it for resets.
Reset mutable session state, including mutable contents of `static readonly` collections. Immutable
constants, cached hashes, and stateless markers do not need artificial reset methods. A stored lambda
can be unsubscribed using the same delegate instance; an anonymous re-created lambda cannot.

`Start` is not a universal readiness barrier for inactive, spawned, or additively loaded objects.
Match cleanup to ownership rather than assuming `OnDestroy` runs for every allocation path. Preserve
unsaved scenes during inspection; validate saved wiring separately from transient runtime fixes.

## Validation

Exercise disable/re-enable, supported scene entry, unload/reload, a failed/overlapping transition,
and a second Play with the project's reload settings. Include destruction/cancellation while work
is pending and pool reuse when applicable. Verify registry/subscriber counts return to the intended
baseline; inspect asset ownership with [Assets](UnityAssetsAndMemoryInstructions.md).

Technical reference: [Awaitable introduction](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/async-awaitable-introduction.html).
Match the reference to the installed engine version when implementing a fix.

Scene placement reference: [Object.Instantiate overloads](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Object.Instantiate.html).
Match the installed engine before recommending an explicit destination-scene overload.

# Unity terrain content audit

Load for owned Terrain/TerrainCollider/TerrainData, runtime height edits or terrain-tile streaming.
Apply the [shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). Establish authoring tools,
data owners, tile layout, rendering pipeline and targets. Keep selected terrain/vegetation systems;
this lens reviews content correctness rather than prescribing a generator.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Tile boundaries | Actual edge heights, neighbor connections, grouping/auto-connect policy | A supported border has a seam or incorrect neighbor/LOD behavior; neighbor links alone do not repair authored height mismatches |
| Height synchronization | CPU/GPU/delayed height writes, supported sync path and subsequent consumers | A required CPU/LOD read observes stale terrain because delayed edits were not synchronized at the owning boundary |
| Collision agreement | TerrainCollider data/holes, visual terrain and live contacts/raycasts | Gameplay collision disagrees with required rendered geometry, including after runtime edits |
| Stream lifetime | Tile replacement/unload, neighbors, actors/navigation and resource ownership | Streaming leaves stale references, broken borders or actors without required collision; general ownership stays in [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Shipped content | TerrainData, layers/materials, tree/detail prototypes and clean load | Missing/unsupported content changes intended terrain in a supported player; verify installed shader/platform support |
| Content scale | Height/detail/tree density, resolution/distances and measured budgets | A target capture exceeds the agreed memory/frame budget; fixed tile sizes or density prescriptions are proposals until measured |

## Interpret with care

Use the installed authoring tool and Editor APIs for asset changes. World generation, vegetation
packages, erosion and custom terrain shaders need their own source-matched review. Rendering cost,
lighting/LOD output and navigation correctness remain owned by their respective lenses; cross-link an
observed failure rather than counting those disciplines as reviewed here.

## Validation

Traverse borders/holes, inspect near/far views, test collision after runtime edits, stream tile cycles,
and reopen saved content. Validate shipped materials/prototypes in a representative player. Missing
live/player checks remain Not verified; a terrain screenshot alone proves neither collision nor streaming.

Technical references: [neighbor contract](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Terrain.SetNeighbors.html)
and [height synchronization](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/TerrainData.SyncHeightmap.html).
These APIs support the boundary checks; exact generator settings and terrain budgets remain project choices.

# Unity testing audit

Load for test quality, behavioral coverage, EditMode/PlayMode selection, or result validation. Apply
[the shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). **Last verified: October 2026.**

Run tests with the repository's runner or `unity-cli` (the `unity:unity-cli` plugin skill); runner
commands live there, not here. Without either, use the Editor's Test Runner window. CI setup lives in
the [CI guide](../ContinuousIntegration/SetupCI.md). Use a test-first workflow skill only when one is
available; this guide checks the tests that exist.

## Establish the baseline

Inventory discovered tests, categories, explicit/expensive exclusions, runner configuration, and
existing failures. Follow current test authorization and any required test-runner subagent. Record
the revision, working-tree changes, engine/package versions, invocation/filter, and result artifacts.
Run the agreed suite; an exit code or "runner started" message alone is insufficient evidence.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Real behavior boundary | Public command, production wiring, assertions | Tests exercise a helper while the broken command path bypasses it |
| Independent expectations | Expected values and fixtures | An assertion's expected value is computed by the production function under test, or a test body contains no assertion (`Assert.*`, `Is.*`, `LogAssert.*`) and calls no helper that throws on failure |
| Failure-sensitive tests | Original bug/rejected operation and asserted consequence | Reverting or breaking the behavior under test leaves the test green. A test with no `Assert` text may assert through a helper: read the helper and confirm it throws on failure before reporting a missing assertion |
| High-value cases | Public commands, state transitions, saves, and lifecycle paths in the reviewed scope | An important supported scenario or prior regression has no failure-sensitive coverage; propose the smallest useful success/rejection/repeat cases where those semantics apply, rather than requiring three tests for every public method |
| Fixture isolation | Objects, scenes, statics, assets, delegates, clocks, randomness | The result changes when the suspect tests run alone, in reverse order, or shuffled (state leaks); list the tests explicitly when the runner has no ordering option |
| Unexpected errors | Console/log handling and allowed messages | Broad suppression hides failures or expected errors are never asserted specifically |
| Asynchronous completion | Timeouts, cancellation, polling conditions, cleanup | A hang is unbounded or success is inferred from a fixed sleep |
| Test discovery | Source inventory of `[Test]`/`[UnityTest]` methods versus the runner's discovered list | A test method in scope is absent from the runner list. Inclusion in a normal player build is owned by [Assemblies](UnityAssemblyDefinitionsInstructions.md); apply its test-inclusion check rather than repeating it here |

## Choose the cheapest meaningful mode

Use EditMode for rules, math, parsers, serialization, and Editor validation when they do not require
a player loop. Use PlayMode for real lifecycle, input integration, scene flow, physics, or runtime UI
wiring. Saved Inspector references and UI command wiring can be valuable integration checks.

EditMode `[UnityTest]` methods advance through `EditorApplication.update`; they can yield `null`
to advance an Editor frame and supported Editor instructions. They do not provide the full PlayMode
coroutine environment. Use `[Test]` for synchronous checks and `[UnityTest]` when yielding is needed.
PlayMode `[UnityTest]` runs as a coroutine. Check the installed Test Framework for supported async
signatures and yield instructions; see the [UnityTest API](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.test-framework@latest/index.html?subfolder=/api/UnityEngine.TestTools.UnityTestAttribute.html).

## Fixtures and coverage

- Inject time, randomness, and external I/O where needed; keep production domain behavior real.
  Assert related effects together when they define one invariant, such as no state change on rejection.
- Clean up even when an assertion fails. Restore changed global settings, detach delegates, destroy
  test-created objects/runtime assets, and dispose handles/token sources using the runner's mode.
- Test temporary save fixtures without touching real player data. For relevant failures, test
  cancellation, re-enable, pool reuse, stale request completion, and a second Play session.
- Report behavioral coverage by important scenario. Passing test count and code coverage percentages
  do not prove saved scene wiring, migration safety, or player experience.
- Recommend a focused set that catches expensive failures. Avoid tests of getters or reversible
  cosmetic edits solely to increase counts. Prefer existing seams before proposing new infrastructure.

## Validation and handoff

Read fresh result XML/logs and report passed, failed, skipped, excluded, undiscovered, and not-run work
with reasons. Preserve known failures as failures. A regression test should fail on the original
behavior when practical, then pass after the fix. Re-run affected integration paths; expand the suite
only when required by project rules or remaining risk.

⚠️ Licence-free CI checks (Tier A in [SetupCI.md](../ContinuousIntegration/SetupCI.md)) inspect project
files and style; they run no Unity tests. A green Tier A result is not test evidence.

Assembly interpretation belongs in [Assemblies](UnityAssemblyDefinitionsInstructions.md), save
scenarios in [Persistence](UnityPersistenceInstructions.md), and async ownership in
[Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md).

Technical reference: [EditMode and PlayMode tests](https://docs.unity.com/en-us/engine/6000.7/manual/programming-environment/test-framework-introduction/getting-started/edit-mode-vs-play-mode-tests)
Check the project's installed Editor and Test Framework versions before changing test assembly or
async setup.

# Unity uGUI audit

Load only for existing or explicitly selected Canvas-based UI (a Canvas, an EventSystem, or
`UnityEngine.UI` usage found in saved scenes, prefabs, or code). In a UI Toolkit project, finding a
Canvas is first a stack/scope question, not authorization to build another UI system. Apply the
[shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). The `unity:ui-ugui` skill, when
available, owns hierarchy/layout work and `unity:optimize-text-mesh-pro` owns font/atlas
implementation; without them, use the project's UI conventions and the official manual.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Input wiring | EventSystem and its input module component, raycasters, camera, blocking graphics | The project uses the Input System package and the EventSystem carries a legacy `StandaloneInputModule` (or no module) instead of `InputSystemUIInputModule`, or a Canvas has no raycaster/camera, and a live click or navigation does not reach the control (confirm with `unity-cli` scene inspection plus a live run) |
| Layout ownership | Anchors, CanvasScaler, LayoutGroups, ContentSizeFitters, LayoutElements | Trace which enabled controllers actually drive each RectTransform property and their axis settings. Report competing writes that cause unstable or incorrect layout (confirm live). LayoutElement supplies sizing information; it is not a second size controller. Stretch anchors and a layout controller can cooperate |
| Listener/row lifetime | Bind/unbind, pool activation, current item identity | A pooled row adds `onClick`/listeners on activate with no removal on deactivate, or acts on an item other than the one it shows (live run: reuse a row twice). Lifetime rules: [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Hide behavior | Canvas/CanvasGroup/GameObject state, nested canvases, scripts | A hidden panel unexpectedly consumes input or performs an action the hide contract forbids, or a shown panel cannot be clicked (confirm live). Background scripts and transparent input blockers may be intentional |
| Domain boundary | UI handler path into authoritative commands | A handler changes domain state without going through the domain command. Ownership rule: [Design](UnityDesignPatternsInstructions.md) |
| Rebuild cost | `Canvas.SendWillRenderCanvases`/`Canvas.BuildBatch` in a capture, per-frame UI writes | A capture attributes excess rebuild/layout time against the agreed workload budget to named writes, or a binding performance rule is violated. Repeating markers and intentional per-frame UI animation alone are candidates |
| Drawing cost | Canvas boundaries, materials/atlases, masking, overdraw | A capture or frame debugger ties a draw-call or fill-cost bottleneck to a named canvas, mask, or material; otherwise record Not verified. Cost standards: [Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md) |

## Interpret with care

- ℹ️ Nested layout groups, UI Animators, Auto Size, forced layout updates, and GameObject deactivation
  can be valid choices. Confirm behavior and cost before recommending alternatives; a universal ban
  hides the cases that need them.
- ℹ️ Splitting canvases can isolate rebuilds but adds batching boundaries. Measure the relevant workload
  before prescribing counts or one canvas per panel. Unity's guidance is to move frequently changing
  elements into their own canvas and profile after each change; see
  [Optimizing Unity UI](https://learn.unity.com/topics/best-practices/guide-optimizing-unity-ui).
- ℹ️ Decorative raycast targets are candidates for removal; a transparent input blocker is intentional.
  Check the actual event path, including nested canvases and the active input module.
- ℹ️ Unity's Input System manual calls `InputSystemUIInputModule` the equivalent of the older
  `StandaloneInputModule`; whether both can coexist is not stated there, so inspect which module the
  EventSystem actually carries. See [Input System UI support](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/UISupport.html).
- ℹ️ Disabling a Canvas does not disable all child scripts, listeners, or nested UI behavior. Verify
  input and lifetime separately. CanvasGroup alpha is not an interaction policy.
- ℹ️ UI updates should reflect changed state through an existing presentation owner. For large lists,
  verify row reuse and current data identity rather than recommending pooling by item-count threshold.
- ℹ️ In Unity's auto layout manual a layout group does not control its own size and a Content Size
  Fitter controls its own element's size per axis; use that to decide which component owns an axis. See
  [auto layout](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.ugui@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/UIAutoLayout.html).

## Validation

Exercise pointer and navigation input, hide/show, scene transitions, pooled/rebound rows, and target
resolutions. Include long strings where localization is supported. Inspect saved prefab overrides
and camera/input references, then profile any claimed rebuild/draw improvement on the target device.

Use [Input](UnityInputSystemInstructions.md) for action ownership and UI/world arbitration,
[Design](UnityDesignPatternsInstructions.md) for command rules, and
[Performance](UnityPerformanceOptimizationInstructions.md) for measurement standards.

# Unity UI Toolkit audit

Load for runtime UXML/USS, data binding, UI lifecycle, input routing, or recycled list items. Apply
[the shared evidence standard](ProjectReview.md#evidence-standard). The `unity:ui` and `unity:ui-uitk`
skills, when available, own layout, styling, custom-element, and binding implementation; without them,
use the project's UI conventions and the official manual. Project naming takes precedence over skill defaults.
**Last verified: October 2026.**

## Establish the live and saved UI

Identify the UIDocument or PanelRenderer (see the [Panel Renderer manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/ui-systems/panel-renderer-component.html)), PanelSettings, source UXML/USS, controller/presenter, runtime data source,
and domain command. Inspect the current visual tree and computed styles when behavior depends on
layout, picking, focus, or propagation (`unity-cli` tree dump, or a live run). Editor binding
(SerializedObject) and runtime binding (data sources) are different systems.

## Audit checks

| Check | Evidence to inspect | Finding when |
|---|---|---|
| Tree lifetime | Creation/rebuild, query timing, cached references | After a re-enable or source replacement, a cached `VisualElement` or query result is not in the current tree (live run: reopen and compare the tree dump) |
| Wiring | UXML names/classes, query type/scope, required references | A name/class the code queries is absent from the UXML and from every builder that creates elements or class names at runtime (the grep is a candidate only: read the helper functions and string-built names first), or an unscoped `Q` returns the first match from a repeated template instance |
| Callback lifetime | `RegisterCallback`, manipulators, `schedule` items | A registration made in bind/enable has no matching unregister/pause on rebind or detach; count registrations after two reopen cycles. Delegate-identity rules: [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) |
| Command ownership | Click/navigation handler path | A handler changes domain state without going through the domain command. Ownership rule: [Design](UnityDesignPatternsInstructions.md) |
| Runtime binding | Data source, property path, binding mode, converter, update trigger | A `DataBinding` has no data source or path that resolves, or the displayed value differs from the source after a change (live run); a two-way write bypasses the command |
| Recycled rows | make/bind/unbind/destroy paths and item identity | A bind path registers item-specific handlers with no unbind counterpart, or the row acts on an item other than the one it shows after sort/remove/scroll (live run) |
| Picking and focus | `picking-mode`, `focusable`/`tabindex`, propagation (`StopPropagation`), pointer capture, picking dump | A `picking-mode: Position` element covers an interactive one, a hidden or transparent element still receives pointer events or focus, or a handler consumes an event another element needs. World/gameplay arbitration: [Input](UnityInputSystemInstructions.md) |
| Layout/style | UXML/USS import log, computed-style dump, shared tokens, inline overrides | An import error prevents intended UI, a selector or inline override breaks a required state/token contract, or a warning identifies a confirmed problem. Unused selectors and computed inline geometry alone are maintenance candidates. Target-resolution correctness needs a live run |
| Update cost | Queries or rebuilds in per-frame callbacks, binding polling, collection growth | A capture ties excess UI refresh/layout time to repeated queries, polling, or rebuilding, or a binding project performance rule is violated; a query or scheduled callback alone is a candidate |

## Cases worth explicit inspection

- ⚠️ Cache the UIDocument (or PanelRenderer) component independently from its visual tree. Bind when the tree is ready
  through the project's supported lifecycle, and re-query after recreation. Another component's
  `OnEnable` is not by itself proof that an arbitrarily ordered document is ready.
- ⚠️ A template's repeated names are valid when queries are scoped to the instance. BEM and kebab-case
  are project conventions; enforce them from [the style guide](../../AgentsInstructions/CodeStyleGuide/UnityStyleGuide.md).
- ⚠️ For recycled rows, register item-independent handlers once where practical, keep current bound
  identity explicit, and detach item-specific observers on unbind. Verify sorting/removal/rebinding.
- ⚠️ In Unity's manual the `binding-path` attribute belongs to the SerializedObject (Editor) binding
  system; runtime data binding binds plain C# objects. A `binding-path` is therefore not evidence of a
  runtime `DataBinding`. Inspect the target property, source path, actual data source, and update mode.
  Two-way binding is appropriate only where writing that property respects the domain contract.
- ⚠️ Runtime binding can poll without `INotifyBindablePropertyChanged`. If notifications/versioning
  are used, verify invalidation of derived properties and source replacement. See
  [runtime data sources](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UIE-runtime-binding-define-data-source.html).
- ⚠️ Test pointer, keyboard, and controller paths where supported. A `ClickEvent` callback does not
  fire for a gamepad Submit, while `Button.clicked` is invoked for both; a handler on `ClickEvent`
  alone leaves controller users unable to press the button. Closing a modal should restore focus and
  input ownership; opacity alone does not establish that hidden content cannot interact. See the
  [Input System UI support](https://docs.unity3d.com/Packages/com.unity.inputsystem@latest/index.html?subfolder=/manual/UISupport.html) page.
- ⚠️ Use `pickingMode` (UXML attribute `picking-mode`) and public class-list APIs such as
  `EnableInClassList` for state. Verify version-sensitive properties against Unity, not a copied CSS
  ban list. See the [VisualElement UXML attributes](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UIE-uxml-element-VisualElement.html).
- ⚠️ USS supports hexadecimal colours (see [USS data types](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UIE-USS-PropertyTypes.html))
  and custom properties (variables); the [custom properties](https://docs.unity3d.com/Manual/UIE-USS-CustomProperties.html)
  page does not state selector-scoping rules, so verify how a variable resolves in the installed
  version before reporting a scope finding. Inline values are legitimate for some computed geometry
  but override stylesheet rules.
- ⚠️ Runtime binding adapters can keep `UnityEngine.UIElements` dependencies out of domain/Core code.
  Use the existing view/callback abstractions after verifying their contracts in the project.

## Validation

Import without relevant UXML/USS errors or warnings. Reopen/re-enable, update and replace the data
source, scroll/sort/remove items, and invoke real commands through supported inputs. Check modal
blocking/focus, empty/error states, target resolutions, and long/localized strings when applicable.
Verify saved UIDocument or PanelRenderer and PanelSettings wiring survives reopening; a runtime-only repair is incomplete
when the feature must ship configured. Static XML parsing is useful but cannot certify Unity rendering.

Use [Scenes](UnityScenesAndLifecycleInstructions.md) for async/tree lifetime,
[Design](UnityDesignPatternsInstructions.md) for domain ownership, and
[Testing](UnityTestingInstructions.md) for integration evidence.

guide_findings.quote: A slider value reaches a dB parameter without conversion
guide_findings.problem: Unqualified Finding-when row conflicts with its own later explicit allowance for a dB-valued slider passed straight through. Literal use can flag a correct implementation.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Require a mismatch between the slider value units/range and exposed parameter units; require conversion only for linear-amplitude input and guard zero when logarithms are used.
guide_findings.evidence: Same file: Unity's own sample can instead use a dB slider and pass it straight through; label the slider contract.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: a collider under a non-uniformly scaled parent has no verified shape
guide_findings.problem: Missing shape verification is categorized as a Finding although router says unavailable geometry checks are Not verified. Nonuniform scale alone supplies no wrong shape or broken behavior evidence.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Mark shape correctness Not verified until inspected; report Finding only for unsupported combination or demonstrated shape/interaction mismatch with intended geometry.
guide_findings.evidence: ProjectReview Evidence standard requires broken behavior/resource contract, budget or binding rule; Physics Validation says unresolved live geometry/contact checks are Not verified.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: The returned count equals the buffer length with no overflow policy
guide_findings.problem: Row makes saturation an automatic defect without requiring completeness. A boolean any-hit consumer may already have sufficient evidence; omission cannot change its true result. Later interpretation correctly limits this to omitted hits affecting correctness.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Qualify with required all-hit/nearest/post-filter semantics and credible omitted-hit consequences; saturation alone is a candidate. An explicitly acceptable truncation contract is sufficient.
guide_findings.evidence: Same file: completeness policy when omitted hits affect correctness. Official RaycastNonAlloc describes truncation, undefined order and potentially nonclosest full results; it does not require every consumer to enumerate all hits. https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Physics.RaycastNonAlloc.html (verified October 2026).
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: `minDistance` is greater than or equal to `maxDistance`
guide_findings.problem: Universal spatial finding ignores rolloff mode and desired audible contract. Current official maxDistance API says logarithmic mode ignores maxDistance; a comparison against an ignored setting alone does not demonstrate positional-audio failure.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Inspect effective rolloff curve and installed engine behavior, then require a violated audible-range/attenuation contract or binding range policy; treat suspicious min/max values as candidates.
guide_findings.evidence: Official AudioSource.maxDistance documents mode-dependent meaning and logarithmic maxDistance being ignored; minDistance identifies the inner nonattenuating region. https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource-maxDistance.html and https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/AudioSource-minDistance.html (Unity 6.6 pages verified October 2026). This confirms overbreadth, not that every engine accepts every reversed setting.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: `Instantiate`/`new GameObject` runs after an additive load without `SceneManager.SetActiveScene` or `MoveGameObjectToScene` while the intended scene is not active
guide_findings.problem: The row's API-presence test misses supported direct destination-scene instantiation. A correctly placed clone can be flagged because neither listed SceneManager call occurs. The global evidence standard mitigates it but contradicts the literal Finding when condition.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Require actual scene ownership or lighting to differ from the intended contract. Inspect destination-scene overloads, InstantiateParameters and parent-driven placement supported by the installed version before flagging missing SetActiveScene/MoveGameObjectToScene.
guide_findings.evidence: Official Object.Instantiate reference (Unity 6.6 page retrieved October 2026) documents Instantiate(original, Scene), explicitly placing the clone in a loaded scene instead of the active scene, plus InstantiateParameters with scene/parent options: https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Object.Instantiate.html . Version-gate these alternatives.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: A capture shows these markers repeating on frames where a script writes text/transform/layout every frame (live profile).
guide_findings.problem: Rebuild cost Finding when requires repetition and correlation, but no demonstrated excess cost or binding performance-rule violation. Cheap intentional animations can satisfy it while meeting budget, contrary to the router's measured-cost standard and UI Toolkit's more precise equivalent.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Treat repeating rebuild markers as candidates; require a capture attributing a measured budget/iteration goal violation to the named writes or a binding project-rule violation before a finding. Otherwise record Checked or a justified proposal.
guide_findings.evidence: ProjectReview.md Evidence standard requires a broken contract, measured budget failure, or binding rule violation; UnityUIToolkitInstructions.md Update cost explicitly requires excess refresh/layout time. This is an internal instruction inconsistency, not a claim that rebuild work is free.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: A component reads another object's or service's state in `Awake`/`OnEnable` where that object is on another GameObject, spawned, inactive, or in another scene, and no bootstrap order, Script Execution Order entry, or explicit initialization call precedes the read
guide_findings.problem: Cross-object access without explicit initialization ordering is a candidate, not proof that the consumed value depends on initialization. Reading an already serialized immutable configuration field does not require the other component's Awake to run first. The literal row overreports this case despite the global evidence standard.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Require that the consumed value actually depends on initialization not guaranteed to precede the read, and identify the unsupported order and consequence. Explicitly permit serialized/default values and other state whose readiness does not depend on that callback.
guide_findings.evidence: Internal contradiction with ProjectReview.md's broken-contract standard. Counterexample: Awake reads another serialized component's inspector-configured constant value and no callback mutates it; lack of Script Execution Order has no demonstrated consequence.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

guide_findings.quote: It is static and read-only: read metadata and serialized references as evidence, never hand-edit them.
guide_findings.problem: The integrity pass labels itself static, but Missing references and Managed-reference types explicitly require Editor queries. This can encourage marking supplied/live evidence unavailable or skipping those rows in a supposedly static pass.
guide_findings.proposed_fix: Describe the pass as read-only with static checks plus Editor-assisted reference/type checks; keep unavailable live rows Not verified without discarding supplied measured evidence.
guide_findings.evidence: Same file: Missing references says Needs a live Editor, and Managed-reference types names SerializationUtility.HasManagedReferencesWithMissingTypes in an Editor query. C09 supplies exactly that evidence.
guide_findings.verification: Corresponding positive and negative corrective cases passed in a fresh session; primary API claims independently checked by parent where relevant.

inputs.evidence: SetDestination returns true. Three frames later pathPending=false and pathStatus=PathPartial. Gameplay awards arrival at the requested shop although the agent stops on the disconnected island edge. All facts are from a fresh player trace.

Actor uses Animator root motion. Agent updatePosition=false, actor writes nextPosition through a documented one-direction adapter. Offscreen, interruption, link, teleport and scene-load checks pass. The only concern is both Animator and NavMeshAgent components exist.

Kinematic sensor has trigger collider and Rigidbody2D. Full Kinematic Contacts=false. Trigger pair works with the intended static sensor target in the installed Editor. All required trigger behavior passes. Reviewer proposes enabling Full Kinematic Contacts everywhere.

2D trigger handler awards contact damage whenever OnTriggerEnter2D runs. A fresh run shows its disabled MonoBehaviour still receives trigger callbacks and awards damage; design explicitly says disabling the script suspends damage.

Single-language game has no localization package. Essential alarm is represented only by red color and sound; supplied user study records missed mandatory alarms for supported muted play and color differentiation settings.

fr-CA table deliberately falls back to fully translated fr. Missing regional cells render the correct approved text. Current largest text and keyboard navigation pass. No project contrast standard is adopted.

NGO 3.1 distributed-authority game intentionally permits owner writes. Receive-side identity/permissions and input rules are enforced. Host/remote/reconnect tests pass. Concern is NetworkVariable writes occur outside a central server.
Door state is sent only in an RPC on unlock, never in replicated state or join snapshot. Fresh late join enters an already unlocked room but sees locked door and cannot proceed.

Producer uses UpdateBefore(Consumer), but producer and consumer are direct children of different sibling groups. Actual Systems window and a development trace show consumer reads last-frame data contrary to same-tick requirement.

ECB creates a temporary entity and adds components to that entity only within that same ECB. Producer dependency completes before framework-managed playback and disposal. Required baked player content passes. Concern is no manual Dispose in consumer code.
Neighbor links point correctly both ways, but two authored adjacent heightmap edges differ by 2m. Fresh traversal shows seam and collision ledge where spec requires continuous ground.

Custom generator uses deferred height updates then supported SyncHeightmap at end of each completed tile edit before CPU consumers. Target captures meet documented budget; density differs from a blog preset.

Manual Cinemachine brain updated once after target movement, supported clocks/cuts pass. Two brains use separate verified channel masks and intended split-screen output. Concern is Manual mode and multiple brains.
Timeline skip disables director before completion callback. Only completion callback restores input/camera owner. Fresh gameplay trace after skip leaves input disabled and cinematic camera active.

inputs.evidence: Two ordered writers set Animator parameter: base locomotion then explicit injury override. Domain deliberately reads Animator state for hit window. All interrupt/cancel/culling checks pass and no binding architecture rule forbids this.
Transition Fixed Duration=false, duration=0.25, source clip takes 4 seconds at current speed. Live measured transition takes 1 second versus project 300ms maximum.
Audio source is paused with Pause. Reclaimer returns source whenever !isPlaying. Fresh trace shows source is returned/reused and original sound cannot resume; requirement is resumable pause.

Pool has immutable mixer group and spatialBlend. All mutable pitch/clip/volume/loop checkout state resets. Mixer exposure is validated at build and Start application succeeds; SetFloat return is not checked at each caller. All audio requirements pass.

Fast discrete body travels more than collider thickness per step, but geometry/speed tests at all supported extremes show required contacts. CCD would increase measured cost; no no-discrete policy exists.

3D obstruction ray starts inside a solid wall. Code expects that ray to return the containing wall and considers clear LOS otherwise. Fixture supplies installed API exclusion and fresh wrong-LOS reproduction.

Owned scene uses only built-in lit materials, lightmaps, LODGroups and skinned characters; no custom passes/shaders/stack. Fresh release player loses baked lighting after required lighting asset omitted.

An intentionally culled unused Render Graph pass has no output consumer; visible output passes. Decorative particles intentionally drop at max capacity without losing essential feedback; all offscreen/pool checks pass.

Addressables layout duplicates a tiny asset deliberately to avoid loading a 200MB shared bundle. Measured loading/memory meet budgets, team documents this choice. Resources contains a 4KB fixed configuration needed at startup.
Audio clip is background-loaded and not ready at first trigger; first mandatory cue arrives 800ms late on target hardware against 100ms budget. Later warmed plays succeed.
Profiler shows main-thread present/wait 12ms, active CPU 3ms, GPU 15ms at 60fps. Proposed optimization replaces three-item Contains with dictionary but has no CPU budget violation.
Default all-layer query intentionally includes every obstacle, and multi-hit result chooses nearest valid hit after filtering. Representative target capture meets budget.
